units.leftText: This is the record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham:
units.rightText: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.

units.leftText: Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers.
units.rightText: Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judah and his brethren;

units.leftText: Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez the father of Hezron, and Hezron the father of Ram.
units.rightText: and Judah begat Perez and Zerah of Tamar; and Perez begat Hezron; and Hezron begat Ram;
leftNotes: 1:3 Greek Aram, a variant of Ram; also in verse 4; see 1 Chronicles 2:9–10|1CH 2:9-10*.

units.leftText: Ram was the father of Amminadab, Amminadab the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon the father of Salmon.
units.rightText: and Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon; and Nahshon begat Salmon;

units.leftText: Salmon was the father of Boaz by Rahab, Boaz the father of Obed by Ruth, Obed the father of Jesse,
units.rightText: and Salmon begat Boaz of Rahab; and Boaz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;

units.leftText: and Jesse the father of David the king. Next: David was the father of Solomon by Uriah’s wife,
units.rightText: and Jesse begat David the king. And David begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Uriah;

units.leftText: Solomon the father of Rehoboam, Rehoboam the father of Abijah, and Abijah the father of Asa.
units.rightText: and Solomon begat Rehoboam; and Rehoboam begat Abijah; and Abijah begat Asa;
leftNotes: 1:7 Greek Asaph, a variant of Asa; also in verse 8; see 1 Chronicles 3:10|1CH 3:10*.

units.leftText: Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat the father of Joram, and Joram the father of Uzziah.
units.rightText: and Asa begat Jehoshaphat; and Jehoshaphat begat Joram; and Joram begat Uzziah;

units.leftText: Uzziah was the father of Jotham, Jotham the father of Ahaz, and Ahaz the father of Hezekiah.
units.rightText: and Uzziah begat Jotham; and Jotham begat Ahaz; and Ahaz begat Hezekiah;

units.leftText: Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh, Manasseh the father of Amon, Amon the father of Josiah,
units.rightText: and Hezekiah begat Manasseh; and Manasseh begat Amon; and Amon begat Josiah;
leftNotes: 1:10 Greek Amōs, a variant spelling of Amon; twice in this verse; see 1 Chronicles 3:14|1CH 3:14*.

units.leftText: and Josiah the father of Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.
units.rightText: and Josiah begat Jechoniah and his brethren, at the time of the carrying away to Babylon.

units.leftText: After the exile to Babylon: Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel, Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel,
units.rightText: And after the carrying away to Babylon, Jechoniah begat Shealtiel; and Shealtiel begat Zerubbabel;

units.leftText: Zerubbabel the father of Abiud, Abiud the father of Eliakim, and Eliakim the father of Azor.
units.rightText: and Zerubbabel begat Abiud; and Abiud begat Eliakim; and Eliakim begat Azor;

units.leftText: Azor was the father of Zadok, Zadok the father of Achim, and Achim the father of Eliud.
units.rightText: and Azor begat Sadoc; and Sadoc begat Achim; and Achim begat Eliud;

units.leftText: Eliud was the father of Eleazar, Eleazar the father of Matthan, Matthan the father of Jacob,
units.rightText: and Eliud begat Eleazar; and Eleazar begat Matthan; and Matthan begat Jacob;

units.leftText: and Jacob the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
units.rightText: and Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

units.leftText: In all, then, there were fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to the Christ. The Birth of Jesus (Isaiah 7:10–16|ISA 7:10-16*; Luke 2:1–7|LUK 2:1-7*)
units.rightText: So all the generations from Abraham unto David are fourteen generations; and from David unto the carrying away to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon unto the Christ fourteen generations.

units.leftText: This is how the birth of Jesus Christ came about: His mother Mary was pledged in marriage to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found with child of the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: Because Joseph her husband was a righteous man and was unwilling to disgrace her publicly, he resolved to divorce her quietly.
units.rightText: And Joseph her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, was minded to put her away privily.

units.leftText: But after he had pondered these things, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to embrace Mary as your wife, for the One conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: But when he thought on these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: She will give birth to a Son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.”
units.rightText: And she shall bring forth a son; and thou shalt call his name JESUS; for it is he that shall save his people from their sins.
leftNotes: 1:21 Jesus means The LORD saves.

units.leftText: All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet:
units.rightText: Now all this is come to pass, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,

units.leftText: “Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and they will call Him Immanuel” ( which means, “God with us” ).
units.rightText: Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, And they shall call his name Immanuel; which is, being interpreted, God with us.
leftNotes: 1:23 Literally they will call His name Immanuel; Isaiah 7:14|ISA 7:14* (see also DSS)
1:23 See Isaiah 7:14|ISA 7:14*, Isaiah 8:8, and Isaiah 8:10.

units.leftText: When Joseph woke up, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and embraced Mary as his wife.
units.rightText: And Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took unto him his wife;

units.leftText: But he had no union with her until she gave birth to a Son. And he gave Him the name Jesus.
units.rightText: and knew her not till she had brought forth a son: and he called his name JESUS.
leftNotes: 1:25 Literally he did not know her

units.leftText: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
units.rightText: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judæa in the days of Herod the king, behold, Wise-men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,

units.leftText: asking, “Where is the One who has been born King of the Jews? We saw His star in the east and have come to worship Him.”
units.rightText: Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we saw his star in the east, and are come to worship him.
leftNotes: 2:2 Or as it rose

units.leftText: When King Herod heard this, he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.
units.rightText: And when Herod the king heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.

units.leftText: And when he had assembled all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he asked them where the Christ was to be born.
units.rightText: And gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Christ should be born.

units.leftText: “In Bethlehem in Judea,” they replied, “for this is what the prophet has written:
units.rightText: And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judæa: for thus it is written through the prophet,

units.leftText: ‘But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah, for out of you will come a ruler who will be the shepherd of My people Israel.’ ”
units.rightText: And thou Bethlehem, land of Judah, Art in no wise least among the princes of Judah: For out of thee shall come forth a governor, Who shall be shepherd of my people Israel.
leftNotes: 2:6 Micah 5:2|MIC 5:2*; see also 2 Samuel 5:2.

units.leftText: Then Herod called the Magi secretly and learned from them the exact time the star had appeared.
units.rightText: Then Herod privily called the Wise-men, and learned of them exactly what time the star appeared.

units.leftText: And sending them to Bethlehem, he said: “Go and search carefully for the Child, and when you find Him, report to me, so that I too may go and worship Him.”
units.rightText: And he sent them to Bethlehem, and said, Go and search out exactly concerning the young child; and when ye have found him, bring me word, that I also may come and worship him.

units.leftText: After they had heard the king, they went on their way, and the star they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it stood over the place where the Child was.
units.rightText: And they, having heard the king, went their way; and lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.

units.leftText: When they saw the star, they rejoiced with great delight.
units.rightText: And when they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.

units.leftText: On coming to the house, they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and worshiped Him. Then they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.
units.rightText: And they came into the house and saw the young child with Mary his mother; and they fell down and worshipped him; and opening their treasures they offered unto him gifts, gold and frankincense and myrrh.

units.leftText: And having been warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they withdrew to their country by another route. The Flight to Egypt (Hosea 11:1–7|HOS 11:1-7*)
units.rightText: And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.

units.leftText: When the Magi had gone, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream. “Get up!” he said. “Take the Child and His mother and flee to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod is going to search for the Child to kill Him.”
units.rightText: Now when they were departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I tell thee: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.

units.leftText: So he got up, took the Child and His mother by night, and withdrew to Egypt,
units.rightText: And he arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt;

units.leftText: where he stayed until the death of Herod. This fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: “Out of Egypt I called My Son.” Weeping and Great Mourning (Jeremiah 31:1–25|JER 31:1-25*)
units.rightText: and was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt did I call my son.

units.leftText: When Herod saw that he had been outwitted by the Magi, he was filled with rage. Sending orders, he put to death all the boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity who were two years old and under, according to the time he had learned from the Magi.
units.rightText: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the Wise-men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the male children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the borders thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had exactly learned of the Wise-men.

units.leftText: Then what was spoken through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled:
units.rightText: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying,

units.leftText: “A voice is heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, because they are no more.” The Return to Nazareth (Luke 2:39–40|LUK 2:39-40*)
units.rightText: A voice was heard in Ramah, Weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; And she would not be comforted, because they are not.
leftNotes: 2:18 Jeremiah 31:15|JER 31:15*

units.leftText: After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt.
units.rightText: But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeareth in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying,

units.leftText: “Get up!” he said. “Take the Child and His mother and go to the land of Israel, for those seeking the Child’s life are now dead.”
units.rightText: Arise and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead that sought the young child’s life.

units.leftText: So Joseph got up, took the Child and His mother, and went to the land of Israel.
units.rightText: And he arose and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.

units.leftText: But when he learned that Archelaus was reigning in Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. And having been warned in a dream, he withdrew to the district of Galilee,
units.rightText: But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judæa in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither; and being warned of God in a dream, he withdrew into the parts of Galilee,

units.leftText: and he went and lived in a town called Nazareth. So was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophets: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
units.rightText: and came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophets, that he should be called a Nazarene.

units.leftText: In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea
units.rightText: And in those days cometh John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judæa, saying,

units.leftText: and saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.”
units.rightText: Repent ye; for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

units.leftText: This is he who was spoken of through the prophet Isaiah: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.’”
units.rightText: For this is he that was spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make ye ready the way of the Lord, Make his paths straight.
leftNotes: 3:3 Isaiah 40:3|ISA 40:3* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: John wore a garment of camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
units.rightText: Now John himself had his raiment of camel’s hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his food was locusts and wild honey.

units.leftText: People went out to him from Jerusalem and all Judea and the whole region around the Jordan.
units.rightText: Then went out unto him Jerusalem, and all Judæa, and all the region round about the Jordan;

units.leftText: Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.
units.rightText: and they were baptized of him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.

units.leftText: But when John saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his place of baptism, he said to them, “You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
units.rightText: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said unto them, Ye offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

units.leftText: Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance.
units.rightText: Bring forth therefore fruit worthy of repentance:

units.leftText: And do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.
units.rightText: and think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

units.leftText: The axe lies ready at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
units.rightText: And even now the axe lieth at the root of the trees: every tree therefore that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

units.leftText: I baptize you with water for repentance, but after me will come One more powerful than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
units.rightText: I indeed baptize you in water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit and in fire:
leftNotes: 3:11 Or in water
3:11 Or in the Holy Spirit and in fire

units.leftText: His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor and to gather His wheat into the barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” The Baptism of Jesus (Mark 1:9–11|MRK 1:9-11*; Luke 3:21–22|LUK 3:21-22*; John 1:29–34|JHN 1:29-34*)
units.rightText: whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing-floor; and he will gather his wheat into the garner, but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire.

units.leftText: At that time Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.
units.rightText: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to the Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.

units.leftText: But John tried to prevent Him, saying, “I need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?”
units.rightText: But John would have hindered him, saying, I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?

units.leftText: “Let it be so now,” Jesus replied. “It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way.” Then John permitted Him.
units.rightText: But Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffereth him.

units.leftText: As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.
units.rightText: And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway from the water: and lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming upon him;
leftNotes: 3:16 NA, BYZ, and TR the heavens were opened to Him
3:16 Or and he saw; see John 1:32–33|JHN 1:32-33*.

units.leftText: And a voice from heaven said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!”
units.rightText: and lo, a voice out of the heavens, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

units.leftText: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
units.rightText: Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.

units.leftText: After fasting forty days and forty nights, He was hungry.
units.rightText: And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he afterward hungered.

units.leftText: The tempter came to Him and said, “If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread.”
units.rightText: And the tempter came and said unto him, If thou art the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’ ”
units.rightText: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
leftNotes: 4:4 Deuteronomy 8:3|DEU 8:3*

units.leftText: Then the devil took Him to the holy city and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple.
units.rightText: Then the devil taketh him into the holy city; and he set him on the pinnacle of the temple,

units.leftText: “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down. For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You, and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’ ”
units.rightText: and saith unto him, If thou art the Son of God, cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee: and, On their hands they shall bear thee up, Lest haply thou dash thy foot against a stone.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’ ”
units.rightText: Jesus said unto him, Again it is written, Thou shalt not make trial of the Lord thy God.
leftNotes: 4:7 Deuteronomy 6:16|DEU 6:16*

units.leftText: Again, the devil took Him to a very high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
units.rightText: Again, the devil taketh him unto an exceeding high mountain, and showeth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;

units.leftText: “All this I will give You,” he said, “if You will fall down and worship me.”
units.rightText: and he said unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.

units.leftText: “Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus told him. “For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’ ”
units.rightText: Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
leftNotes: 4:10 Deuteronomy 6:13|DEU 6:13*

units.leftText: Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him. Jesus Begins His Ministry (Isaiah 9:1–7|ISA 9:1-7*; Mark 1:14–15|MRK 1:14-15*; Luke 4:14–15|LUK 4:14-15*)
units.rightText: Then the devil leaveth him; and behold, angels came and ministered unto him.

units.leftText: When Jesus heard that John had been imprisoned, He withdrew to Galilee.
units.rightText: Now when he heard that John was delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee;

units.leftText: Leaving Nazareth, He went and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,
units.rightText: and leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali:

units.leftText: to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:
units.rightText: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,

units.leftText: “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles —
units.rightText: The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, Toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,

units.leftText: the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.”
units.rightText: The people that sat in darkness Saw a great light, And to them that sat in the region and shadow of death, To them did light spring up.

units.leftText: From that time on Jesus began to preach, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.” The First Disciples (Mark 1:16–20|MRK 1:16-20*; Luke 5:1–11|LUK 5:1-11*; John 1:35–42|JHN 1:35-42*)
units.rightText: From that time began Jesus to preach, and to say, Repent ye; for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

units.leftText: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
units.rightText: And walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brethren, Simon who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishers.

units.leftText: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you fishers of men.

units.leftText: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
units.rightText: And they straightway left the nets, and followed him.

units.leftText: Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. Jesus called them,
units.rightText: And going on from thence he saw two other brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.

units.leftText: and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him. Jesus Heals the Multitudes (Mark 3:7–12|MRK 3:7-12*; Luke 6:17–19|LUK 6:17-19*)
units.rightText: And they straightway left the boat and their father, and followed him.

units.leftText: Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.
units.rightText: And Jesus went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of disease and all manner of sickness among the people.

units.leftText: News about Him spread all over Syria, and people brought to Him all who were ill with various diseases, those suffering acute pain, the demon-possessed, those having seizures, and the paralyzed, and He healed them.
units.rightText: And the report of him went forth into all Syria: and they brought unto him all that were sick, holden with divers diseases and torments, possessed with demons, and epileptic, and palsied; and he healed them.

units.leftText: Large crowds followed Him, having come from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.
units.rightText: And there followed him great multitudes from Galilee and Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judæa and from beyond the Jordan.
leftNotes: 4:25 That is, the Ten Cities

units.leftText: When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on the mountain and sat down. His disciples came to Him,
units.rightText: And seeing the multitudes, he went up into the mountain: and when he had sat down, his disciples came unto him:

units.leftText: and He began to teach them, saying: The Beatitudes (Psalm 1:1–6|PSA 1:1-6*; Luke 6:20–23|LUK 6:20-23*)
units.rightText: and he opened his mouth and taught them, saying,

units.leftText: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
units.rightText: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
units.rightText: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

units.leftText: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
units.rightText: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
leftNotes: 5:5 Or Blessed are those who exercise strength under control, for they will inherit the land; see Psalm 37:11|PSA 37:11*.

units.leftText: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
units.rightText: Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.

units.leftText: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
units.rightText: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

units.leftText: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
units.rightText: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

units.leftText: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.
units.rightText: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called sons of God.

units.leftText: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
units.rightText: Blessed are they that have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me.
units.rightText: Blessed are ye when men shall reproach you, and persecute you, and say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.

units.leftText: Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets before you. Salt and Light (Mark 9:49–50|MRK 9:49-50*; Luke 14:34–35|LUK 14:34-35*; Philippians 2:12–18|PHP 2:12-18*)
units.rightText: Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets that were before you.

units.leftText: You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its savor, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by men.
units.rightText: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost its savor, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under foot of men.

units.leftText: You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.
units.rightText: Ye are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hid.
leftNotes: 5:14 Literally A city lying on a hill

units.leftText: Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a basket. Instead, they set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
units.rightText: Neither do men light a lamp, and put it under the bushel, but on the stand; and it shineth unto all that are in the house.

units.leftText: In the same way, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven. The Fulfillment of the Law
units.rightText: Even so let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

units.leftText: Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them.
units.rightText: Think not that I came to destroy the law or the prophets: I came not to destroy, but to fulfil.

units.leftText: For I tell you truly, until heaven and earth pass away, not a single jot, not a stroke of a pen, will disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished.
units.rightText: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass away, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass away from the law, till all things be accomplished.

units.leftText: So then, whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do likewise will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever practices and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
units.rightText: Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven. Anger and Reconciliation (Luke 12:57–59|LUK 12:57-59*)
units.rightText: For I say unto you, that except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no wise enter into the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not murder’ and ‘Anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.’
units.rightText: Ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment:
leftNotes: 5:21 Exodus 20:13|EXO 20:13*; Deuteronomy 5:17

units.leftText: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be subject to the Sanhedrin. But anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be subject to the fire of hell.
units.rightText: but I say unto you, that every one who is angry with his brother shall be in danger of the judgment; and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council; and whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of the hell of fire.
leftNotes: 5:22 BYZ and TR include without cause.
5:22 Raca is an Aramaic expression of contempt.
5:22 Or the Council
5:22 Or the hell of fire; Greek the Gehenna of fire

units.leftText: So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
units.rightText: If therefore thou art offering thy gift at the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath aught against thee,

units.leftText: leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.
units.rightText: leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way, first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.

units.leftText: Reconcile quickly with your adversary, while you are still on the way to court. Otherwise, he may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.
units.rightText: Agree with thine adversary quickly, while thou art with him in the way; lest haply the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny. Adultery (Leviticus 18:1–30|LEV 18:1-30*)
units.rightText: Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou have paid the last farthing.
leftNotes: 5:26 Greek kodrantēn; that is, a Roman copper coin worth about 1/64 of a denarius

units.leftText: You have heard that it was said, ‘Do not commit adultery.’
units.rightText: Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt not commit adultery:
leftNotes: 5:27 Exodus 20:14|EXO 20:14*; Deuteronomy 5:18

units.leftText: But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
units.rightText: but I say unto you, that every one that looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.

units.leftText: If your right eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
units.rightText: And if thy right eye causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body be cast into hell.
leftNotes: 5:29 Greek Gehenna; also in verse 30

units.leftText: And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to depart into hell. Divorce (Deuteronomy 24:1–5|DEU 24:1-5*; Luke 16:18|LUK 16:18*)
units.rightText: And if thy right hand causeth thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body go into hell.

units.leftText: It has also been said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’
units.rightText: It was said also, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:
leftNotes: 5:31 Deuteronomy 24:1|DEU 24:1*

units.leftText: But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, brings adultery upon her. And he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery. Oaths and Vows (Numbers 30:1–16|NUM 30:1-16*)
units.rightText: but I say unto you, that every one that putteth away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, maketh her an adulteress: and whosoever shall marry her when she is put away committeth adultery.
leftNotes: 5:32 Or causes her to commit adultery

units.leftText: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your vows to the Lord.’
units.rightText: Again, ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:
leftNotes: 5:33 Numbers 30:2|NUM 30:2*

units.leftText: But I tell you not to swear at all: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne;
units.rightText: but I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by the heaven, for it is the throne of God;

units.leftText: or by the earth, for it is His footstool; or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
units.rightText: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.

units.leftText: Nor should you swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.
units.rightText: Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, for thou canst not make one hair white or black.

units.leftText: Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’ Anything more comes from the evil one. Love Your Enemies (Leviticus 24:17–23|LEV 24:17-23*; Luke 6:27–36|LUK 6:27-36*)
units.rightText: But let your speech be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: and whatsoever is more than these is of the evil one.
leftNotes: 5:37 Or from evil

units.leftText: You have heard that it was said, ‘Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.’
units.rightText: Ye have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:
leftNotes: 5:38 Exodus 21:24|EXO 21:24*; Leviticus 24:20; Deuteronomy 19:21

units.leftText: But I tell you not to resist an evil person. If someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also;
units.rightText: but I say unto you, Resist not him that is evil: but whosoever smiteth thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

units.leftText: if someone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well;
units.rightText: And if any man would go to law with thee, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also.

units.leftText: and if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles.
units.rightText: And whosoever shall compel thee to go one mile, go with him two.
leftNotes: 5:41 Greek one milion; that is, a Roman mile, approximately 4,855 feet or 1,480 meters
5:41 Literally go with him two.

units.leftText: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.
units.rightText: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

units.leftText: You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor’ and ‘Hate your enemy.’
units.rightText: Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt love thy neighbor, and hate thine enemy:
leftNotes: 5:43 Leviticus 19:18|LEV 19:18*

units.leftText: But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
units.rightText: but I say unto you, Love your enemies, and pray for them that persecute you;
leftNotes: 5:44 BYZ and TR love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who spitefully accuse you and persecute you; see Luke 6:27–28|LUK 6:27-28*.

units.leftText: that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
units.rightText: that ye may be sons of your Father who is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sendeth rain on the just and the unjust.

units.leftText: If you love those who love you, what reward will you get? Do not even tax collectors do the same?
units.rightText: For if ye love them that love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?

units.leftText: And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing more than others? Do not even Gentiles do the same?
units.rightText: And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the Gentiles the same?

units.leftText: Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.[’’]
units.rightText: Ye therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

units.leftText: “Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
units.rightText: Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men, to be seen of them: else ye have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.
leftNotes: 6:1 BYZ and TR charitable acts or alms

units.leftText: So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
units.rightText: When therefore thou doest alms, sound not a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.

units.leftText: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
units.rightText: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

units.leftText: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you. The Lord’s Prayer (Luke 11:1–4|LUK 11:1-4*)
units.rightText: that thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.

units.leftText: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
units.rightText: And when ye pray, ye shall not be as the hypocrites: for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.

units.leftText: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
units.rightText: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thine inner chamber, and having shut thy door, pray to thy Father who is in secret, and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.

units.leftText: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.
units.rightText: And in praying use not vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

units.leftText: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.
units.rightText: Be not therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

units.leftText: So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.
units.rightText: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

units.leftText: Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
units.rightText: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.

units.leftText: Give us this day our daily bread.
units.rightText: Give us this day our daily bread.

units.leftText: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
units.rightText: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.

units.leftText: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. ’
units.rightText: And bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.
leftNotes: 6:13 Or from evil; BYZ and TR include For Yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory, forever. Amen.

units.leftText: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
units.rightText: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

units.leftText: But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours. Proper Fasting
units.rightText: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

units.leftText: When you fast, do not be somber like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
units.rightText: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen of men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.

units.leftText: But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
units.rightText: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thy head, and wash thy face;

units.leftText: so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you. Treasures in Heaven (Luke 12:32–34|LUK 12:32-34*)
units.rightText: that thou be not seen of men to fast, but of thy Father who is in secret: and thy Father, who seeth in secret, shall recompense thee.

units.leftText: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
units.rightText: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal:
leftNotes: 6:19 Or worm; also in verse 20

units.leftText: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moth and rust do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.
units.rightText: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth consume, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

units.leftText: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. The Lamp of the Body (Luke 11:33–36|LUK 11:33-36*)
units.rightText: for where thy treasure is, there will thy heart be also.

units.leftText: The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.
units.rightText: The lamp of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
leftNotes: 6:22 Literally If your eye is sound; see Proverbs 22:9|PRO 22:9*

units.leftText: But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
units.rightText: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is the darkness!
leftNotes: 6:23 Literally if your eye is evil; see Proverbs 23:6|PRO 23:6* and Proverbs 28:22

units.leftText: No one can serve two masters: Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money. Do Not Worry (Luke 12:22–31|LUK 12:22-31*)
units.rightText: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

units.leftText: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
units.rightText: Therefore I say unto you, Be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than the food, and the body than the raiment?

units.leftText: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?
units.rightText: Behold the birds of the heaven, that they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; and your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are not ye of much more value than they?

units.leftText: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
units.rightText: And which of you by being anxious can add one cubit unto the measure of his life?
leftNotes: 6:27 Or a single cubit to his height; a cubit was approximately 18 inches or 45 centimeters.

units.leftText: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.
units.rightText: And why are ye anxious concerning raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

units.leftText: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
units.rightText: yet I say unto you, that even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

units.leftText: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?
units.rightText: But if God doth so clothe the grass of the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?

units.leftText: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’
units.rightText: Be not therefore anxious, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

units.leftText: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
units.rightText: For after all these things do the Gentiles seek; for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.

units.leftText: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.
units.rightText: But seek ye first his kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
leftNotes: 6:33 SBL, WH, and NE seek first His kingdom; see also Luke 12:31|LUK 12:31*.

units.leftText: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.[’’]
units.rightText: Be not therefore anxious for the morrow: for the morrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

units.leftText: “Do not judge, or you will be judged.
units.rightText: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

units.leftText: For with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.
units.rightText: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured unto you.

units.leftText: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
units.rightText: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

units.leftText: How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while there is still a beam in your own eye?
units.rightText: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me cast out the mote out of thine eye; and lo, the beam is in thine own eye?

units.leftText: You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
units.rightText: Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.

units.leftText: Do not give dogs what is holy; do not throw your pearls before swine. If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces. Ask, Seek, Knock (Luke 11:5–13|LUK 11:5-13*)
units.rightText: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast your pearls before the swine, lest haply they trample them under their feet, and turn and rend you.

units.leftText: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
units.rightText: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

units.leftText: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
units.rightText: for every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

units.leftText: Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?
units.rightText: Or what man is there of you, who, if his son shall ask him for a loaf, will give him a stone;

units.leftText: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?
units.rightText: or if he shall ask for a fish, will give him a serpent?

units.leftText: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!
units.rightText: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father who is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

units.leftText: In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets. The Narrow Gate (Luke 13:22–30|LUK 13:22-30*)
units.rightText: All things therefore whatsoever ye would that men should do unto you, even so do ye also unto them: for this is the law and the prophets.

units.leftText: Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
units.rightText: Enter ye in by the narrow gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many are they that enter in thereby.

units.leftText: But small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and only a few find it. A Tree and Its Fruit (Luke 6:43–45|LUK 6:43-45*)
units.rightText: For narrow is the gate, and straitened the way, that leadeth unto life, and few are they that find it.

units.leftText: Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
units.rightText: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.

units.leftText: By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
units.rightText: By their fruits ye shall know them. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

units.leftText: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.
units.rightText: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but the corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

units.leftText: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.
units.rightText: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

units.leftText: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
units.rightText: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

units.leftText: So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.
units.rightText: Therefore by their fruits ye shall know them.

units.leftText: Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.
units.rightText: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father who is in heaven.

units.leftText: Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?’
units.rightText: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy by thy name, and by thy name cast out demons, and by thy name do many mighty works?

units.leftText: Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!’ The House on the Rock (Luke 6:46–49|LUK 6:46-49*)
units.rightText: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

units.leftText: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
units.rightText: Every one therefore that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them, shall be likened unto a wise man, who built his house upon the rock:

units.leftText: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.
units.rightText: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon the rock.

units.leftText: But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
units.rightText: And every one that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, who built his house upon the sand:

units.leftText: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell— and great was its collapse!” The Authority of Jesus
units.rightText: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and smote upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall thereof.

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at His teaching,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching:

units.leftText: because He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.
units.rightText: for he taught them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.

units.leftText: When Jesus came down from the mountain, large crowds followed Him.
units.rightText: And when he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

units.leftText: Suddenly a leper came and knelt before Him, saying, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”
units.rightText: And behold, there came to him a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
leftNotes: 8:2 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
units.rightText: And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou made clean. And straightway his leprosy was cleansed.

units.leftText: Then Jesus instructed him, “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift prescribed by Moses, as a testimony to them.” The Faith of the Centurion (Luke 7:1–10|LUK 7:1-10*; John 4:43–54|JHN 4:43-54*)
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
leftNotes: 8:4 See Leviticus 14:1–32|LEV 14:1-32*.

units.leftText: When Jesus had entered Capernaum, a centurion came and pleaded with Him,
units.rightText: And when he was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,

units.leftText: “Lord, my servant lies at home, paralyzed and in terrible agony.”
units.rightText: and saying, Lord, my servant lieth in the house sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.
leftNotes: 8:6 Or child; also in verses 8 and 13

units.leftText: “I will go and heal him,” Jesus replied.
units.rightText: And he saith unto him, I will come and heal him.

units.leftText: The centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy to have You come under my roof. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
units.rightText: And the centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.

units.leftText: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”
units.rightText: For I also am a man under authority, having under myself soldiers: and I say to this one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.

units.leftText: When Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those following Him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.
units.rightText: And when Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

units.leftText: I say to you that many will come from the east and the west to share the banquet with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
units.rightText: And I say unto you, that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven:

units.leftText: But the sons of the kingdom will be thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
units.rightText: but the sons of the kingdom shall be cast forth into the outer darkness: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to the centurion, “Go! As you have believed, so will it be done for you.” And his servant was healed at that very hour. Jesus Heals at Peter’s House (Mark 1:29–34|MRK 1:29-34*; Luke 4:38–41|LUK 4:38-41*)
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And the servant was healed in that hour.

units.leftText: When Jesus arrived at Peter’s house, He saw Peter’s mother-in-law sick in bed with a fever.
units.rightText: And when Jesus was come into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother lying sick of a fever.

units.leftText: So He touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she got up and began to serve Him.
units.rightText: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she arose, and ministered unto him.

units.leftText: When evening came, many who were demon-possessed were brought to Jesus, and He drove out the spirits with a word and healed all the sick.
units.rightText: And when even was come, they brought unto him many possessed with demons: and he cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all that were sick:

units.leftText: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah: “He took up our infirmities and carried our diseases.” The Cost of Discipleship (Luke 9:57–62|LUK 9:57-62*; Luke 14:25–33|LUK 14:25-33*; John 6:59–66|JHN 6:59-66*)
units.rightText: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our diseases.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw a large crowd around Him, He gave orders to cross to the other side of the sea.
units.rightText: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandment to depart unto the other side.
leftNotes: 8:18 That is, the Sea of Galilee; Greek to the other side

units.leftText: And one of the scribes came to Him and said, “Teacher, I will follow You wherever You go.”
units.rightText: And there came a scribe, and said unto him, Teacher, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the heaven have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

units.leftText: Another of His disciples requested, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
units.rightText: And another of the disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.

units.leftText: But Jesus told him, “Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead.” Jesus Calms the Storm (Psalm 107:1–43|PSA 107:1-43*; Mark 4:35–41|MRK 4:35-41*; Luke 8:22–25|LUK 8:22-25*)
units.rightText: But Jesus saith unto him, Follow me; and leave the dead to bury their own dead.

units.leftText: When He got into the boat, His disciples followed Him.
units.rightText: And when he was entered into a boat, his disciples followed him.

units.leftText: Suddenly a violent storm came up on the sea, so that the boat was engulfed by the waves. But Jesus was sleeping.
units.rightText: And behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the boat was covered with the waves: but he was asleep.

units.leftText: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Lord, save us! We are perishing!”
units.rightText: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Save, Lord; we perish.

units.leftText: “You of little faith,” Jesus replied, “why are you so afraid?” Then He got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and it was perfectly calm.
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.

units.leftText: The men were amazed and asked, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the sea obey Him!” The Demons and the Pigs (Mark 5:1–20|MRK 5:1-20*; Luke 8:26–39|LUK 8:26-39*)
units.rightText: And the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?

units.leftText: When Jesus arrived on the other side in the region of the Gadarenes, He was met by two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs. They were so violent that no one could pass that way.
units.rightText: And when he was come to the other side into the country of the Gadarenes, there met him two possessed with demons, coming forth out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man could pass by that way.
leftNotes: 8:28 BYZ, TR, and PT Gergesenes; other manuscripts Gerasenes

units.leftText: “What do You want with us, Son of God?” they shouted. “Have You come here to torture us before the appointed time?”
units.rightText: And behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?

units.leftText: In the distance a large herd of pigs was feeding.
units.rightText: Now there was afar off from them a herd of many swine feeding.

units.leftText: So the demons begged Jesus, “If You drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”
units.rightText: And the demons besought him, saying, If thou cast us out, send us away into the herd of swine.

units.leftText: “Go!” He told them. So they came out and went into the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Go. And they came out, and went into the swine: and behold, the whole herd rushed down the steep into the sea, and perished in the waters.

units.leftText: Those tending the pigs ran off into the town and reported all this, including the account of the demon-possessed men.
units.rightText: And they that fed them fled, and went away into the city, and told everything, and what was befallen to them that were possessed with demons.

units.leftText: Then the whole town went out to meet Jesus. And when they saw Him, they begged Him to leave their region.
units.rightText: And behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart from their borders.

units.leftText: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to His own town.
units.rightText: And he entered into a boat, and crossed over, and came into his own city.

units.leftText: Just then some men brought to Him a paralytic lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.”
units.rightText: And behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, be of good cheer; thy sins are forgiven.
leftNotes: 9:2 Literally And behold, they brought

units.leftText: On seeing this, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming!”
units.rightText: And behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemeth.

units.leftText: But Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?
units.rightText: And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?
leftNotes: 9:4 NA, BYZ, and TR saw

units.leftText: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
units.rightText: For which is easier, to say, Thy sins are forgiven; or to say, Arise, and walk?

units.leftText: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” Then He said to the paralytic, “Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
units.rightText: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath authority on earth to forgive sins (then saith he to the sick of the palsy), Arise, and take up thy bed, and go unto thy house.

units.leftText: And the man got up and went home.
units.rightText: And he arose, and departed to his house.

units.leftText: When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men. Jesus Calls Matthew (Mark 2:13–17|MRK 2:13-17*; Luke 5:27–32|LUK 5:27-32*)
units.rightText: But when the multitudes saw it, they were afraid, and glorified God, who had given such authority unto men.

units.leftText: As Jesus went on from there, He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Matthew got up and followed Him.
units.rightText: And as Jesus passed by from thence, he saw a man, called Matthew, sitting at the place of toll: and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.

units.leftText: Later, as Jesus was dining at Matthew’s house, many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Him and His disciples.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with Jesus and his disciples.

units.leftText: When the Pharisees saw this, they asked His disciples, “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
units.rightText: And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Teacher with the publicans and sinners?

units.leftText: On hearing this, Jesus said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
units.rightText: But when he heard it, he said, They that are whole have no need of a physician, but they that are sick.

units.leftText: But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners. ” Questions about Fasting (Mark 2:18–20|MRK 2:18-20*; Luke 5:33–35|LUK 5:33-35*)
units.rightText: But go ye and learn what this meaneth, I desire mercy, and not sacrifice: for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.
leftNotes: 9:13 Hosea 6:6|HOS 6:6*
9:13 BYZ and TR but sinners, to repentance; see Luke 5:32|LUK 5:32*.

units.leftText: Then John’s disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast so often, but Your disciples do not fast?”
units.rightText: Then come to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast oft, but thy disciples fast not?
leftNotes: 9:14 NE and WH do not include so often.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom mourn while He is with them? But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast. The Patches and the Wineskins (Mark 2:21–22|MRK 2:21-22*; Luke 5:36–39|LUK 5:36-39*)
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, Can the sons of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then will they fast.

units.leftText: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. For the patch will pull away from the garment, and a worse tear will result.
units.rightText: And no man putteth a piece of undressed cloth upon an old garment; for that which should fill it up taketh from the garment, and a worse rent is made.

units.leftText: Neither do men pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will burst, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.” The Healing Touch of Jesus (Mark 5:21–43|MRK 5:21-43*; Luke 8:40–56|LUK 8:40-56*)
units.rightText: Neither do men put new wine into old wine-skins: else the skins burst, and the wine is spilled, and the skins perish: but they put new wine into fresh wine-skins, and both are preserved.

units.leftText: While Jesus was saying these things, a synagogue leader came and knelt before Him. “My daughter has just died,” he said. “But come and place Your hand on her, and she will live.”
units.rightText: While he spake these things unto them, behold, there came a ruler, and worshipped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay thy hand upon her, and she shall live.

units.leftText: So Jesus got up and went with him, along with His disciples.
units.rightText: And Jesus arose, and followed him, and so did his disciples.

units.leftText: Suddenly a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years came up behind Him and touched the fringe of His cloak.
units.rightText: And behold, a woman, who had an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the border of his garment:

units.leftText: She said to herself, “If only I touch His cloak, I will be healed.”
units.rightText: for she said within herself, If I do but touch his garment, I shall be made whole.

units.leftText: Jesus turned and saw her. “Take courage, daughter,” He said, “your faith has healed you.” And the woman was healed from that very hour.
units.rightText: But Jesus turning and seeing her said, Daughter, be of good cheer; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.

units.leftText: When Jesus entered the house of the synagogue leader, He saw the flute players and the noisy crowd.
units.rightText: And when Jesus came into the ruler’s house, and saw the flute-players, and the crowd making a tumult,

units.leftText: “Go away,” He told them. “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” And they laughed at Him.
units.rightText: he said, Give place: for the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.

units.leftText: After the crowd had been put outside, Jesus went in and took the girl by the hand, and she got up.
units.rightText: But when the crowd was put forth, he entered in, and took her by the hand; and the damsel arose.

units.leftText: And the news about this spread throughout that region. Jesus Heals the Blind and Mute (Mark 7:31–37|MRK 7:31-37*)
units.rightText: And the fame hereof went forth into all that land.

units.leftText: As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed Him, crying out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”
units.rightText: And as Jesus passed by from thence, two blind men followed him, crying out, and saying, Have mercy on us, thou son of David.

units.leftText: After Jesus had entered the house, the blind men came to Him. “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” He asked. “Yes, Lord,” they answered.
units.rightText: And when he was come into the house, the blind men came to him: and Jesus saith unto them, Believe ye that I am able to do this? They say unto him, Yea, Lord.

units.leftText: Then He touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith will it be done to you.”
units.rightText: Then touched he their eyes, saying, According to your faith be it done unto you.

units.leftText: And their eyes were opened. Jesus warned them sternly, “See that no one finds out about this!”
units.rightText: And their eyes were opened. And Jesus strictly charged them, saying, See that no man know it.

units.leftText: But they went out and spread the news about Him throughout the land.
units.rightText: But they went forth, and spread abroad his fame in all that land.

units.leftText: As they were leaving, a demon-possessed man who was mute was brought to Jesus.
units.rightText: And as they went forth, behold, there was brought to him a dumb man possessed with a demon.

units.leftText: And when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”
units.rightText: And when the demon was cast out, the dumb man spake: and the multitudes marvelled, saying, It was never so seen in Israel.

units.leftText: But the Pharisees said, “It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons.” The Lord of the Harvest (Luke 10:1–12|LUK 10:1-12*)
units.rightText: But the Pharisees said, By the prince of the demons casteth he out demons.

units.leftText: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness.
units.rightText: And Jesus went about all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of disease and all manner of sickness.

units.leftText: When He saw the crowds, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
units.rightText: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were distressed and scattered, as sheep not having a shepherd.

units.leftText: Then He said to His disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
units.rightText: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest indeed is plenteous, but the laborers are few.

units.leftText: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.”
units.rightText: Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he send forth laborers into his harvest.

units.leftText: And calling His twelve disciples to Him, Jesus gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they could drive them out and heal every disease and sickness.
units.rightText: And he called unto him his twelve disciples, and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of disease and all manner of sickness.

units.leftText: These are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John;
units.rightText: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;

units.leftText: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
units.rightText: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphæus, and Thaddæus;

units.leftText: Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus. The Ministry of the Twelve (Mark 6:7–13|MRK 6:7-13*; Luke 9:1–6|LUK 9:1-6*)
units.rightText: Simon the Cananæan, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
leftNotes: 10:4 Greek Simon the Cananean
10:4 Literally the one also having betrayed Him

units.leftText: These twelve Jesus sent out with the following instructions: “Do not go onto the road of the Gentiles or enter any town of the Samaritans.
units.rightText: These twelve Jesus sent forth, and charged them, saying, Go not into any way of the Gentiles, and enter not into any city of the Samaritans:

units.leftText: Go rather to the lost sheep of Israel.
units.rightText: but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

units.leftText: As you go, preach this message: ‘The kingdom of heaven is near.’
units.rightText: And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.

units.leftText: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons. Freely you have received; freely give.
units.rightText: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons: freely ye received, freely give.
leftNotes: 10:8 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: Do not take along any gold or silver or copper in your belts.
units.rightText: Get you no gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses;

units.leftText: Take no bag for the road, or second tunic, or sandals, or staff; for the worker is worthy of his provisions.
units.rightText: no wallet for your journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.
