units.leftText: Whatever town or village you enter, find out who is worthy there and stay at his house until you move on.
units.rightText: And into whatsoever city or village ye shall enter, search out who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go forth.
leftNotes: 10:11 Literally stay there

units.leftText: As you enter the home, greet its occupants.
units.rightText: And as ye enter into the house, salute it.
leftNotes: 10:12 Literally greet it

units.leftText: If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it, but if it is not, let your peace return to you.
units.rightText: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.

units.leftText: And if anyone will not welcome you or heed your words, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that home or town.
units.rightText: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, as ye go forth out of that house or that city, shake off the dust of your feet.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town. Sheep among Wolves (2 Timothy 1:3–12|2TI 1:3-12*)
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment, than for that city.

units.leftText: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.
units.rightText: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.

units.leftText: But beware of men, for they will hand you over to their councils and flog you in their synagogues.
units.rightText: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you;

units.leftText: On My account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.
units.rightText: yea and before governors and kings shall ye be brought for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.

units.leftText: But when they hand you over, do not worry about how to respond or what to say. In that hour you will be given what to say.
units.rightText: But when they deliver you up, be not anxious how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that hour what ye shall speak.

units.leftText: For it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
units.rightText: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.

units.leftText: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.
units.rightText: And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his child: and children shall rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.

units.leftText: You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.
units.rightText: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.

units.leftText: When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next. Truly I tell you, you will not reach all the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
units.rightText: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone through the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.

units.leftText: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.
units.rightText: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.

units.leftText: It is enough for a disciple to be like his teacher, and a servant like his master. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household! Fear God Alone (Luke 12:4–7|LUK 12:4-7*)
units.rightText: It is enough for the disciple that he be as his teacher, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more them of his household!
leftNotes: 10:25 WH Beezeboul; Vulgate Beelzebub

units.leftText: So do not be afraid of them. For there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
units.rightText: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.

units.leftText: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops.
units.rightText: What I tell you in the darkness, speak ye in the light; and what ye hear in the ear, proclaim upon the house-tops.

units.leftText: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
units.rightText: And be not afraid of them that kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
leftNotes: 10:28 Greek Gehenna

units.leftText: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.
units.rightText: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? and not one of them shall fall on the ground without your Father:
leftNotes: 10:29 Greek an assarion; that is, a Roman copper coin worth about 1/16 of a denarius

units.leftText: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
units.rightText: but the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

units.leftText: So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. Confessing Christ (Luke 12:8–12|LUK 12:8-12*)
units.rightText: Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.

units.leftText: Therefore everyone who confesses Me before men, I will also confess him before My Father in heaven.
units.rightText: Every one therefore who shall confess me before men, him will I also confess before my Father who is in heaven.

units.leftText: But whoever denies Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father in heaven. Not Peace but a Sword (Micah 7:1–6|MIC 7:1-6*; Luke 12:49–53|LUK 12:49-53*)
units.rightText: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father who is in heaven.

units.leftText: Do not assume that I have come to bring peace to the earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword.
units.rightText: Think not that I came to send peace on the earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.

units.leftText: For I have come to turn ‘a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
units.rightText: For I came to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law:

units.leftText: A man’s enemies will be the members of his own household.’
units.rightText: and a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.

units.leftText: Anyone who loves his father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; anyone who loves his son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me;
units.rightText: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

units.leftText: and anyone who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me.
units.rightText: And he that doth not take his cross and follow after me, is not worthy of me.

units.leftText: Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for My sake will find it. The Reward of Service (2 Kings 4:8–17|2KI 4:8-17*)
units.rightText: He that findeth his life shall lose it; and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.

units.leftText: He who receives you receives Me, and he who receives Me receives the One who sent Me.
units.rightText: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.

units.leftText: Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous man because he is a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.
units.rightText: He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward: and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward.

units.leftText: And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is My disciple, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.”
units.rightText: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only, in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you he shall in no wise lose his reward.

units.leftText: After Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He went on from there to teach and preach in their cities.
units.rightText: And it came to pass when Jesus had finished commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and preach in their cities.
leftNotes: 11:1 That is, in the towns of Galilee

units.leftText: Meanwhile John heard in prison about the works of Christ, and he sent his disciples
units.rightText: Now when John heard in the prison the works of the Christ, he sent by his disciples
leftNotes: 11:2 BYZ and TR he sent two of his disciples

units.leftText: to ask Him, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”
units.rightText: and said unto him, Art thou he that cometh, or look we for another?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Go back and report to John what you hear and see:
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and tell John the things which ye hear and see:

units.leftText: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
units.rightText: the blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised up, and the poor have good tidings preached to them.
leftNotes: 11:5 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me. ” Jesus Testifies about John (Malachi 3:1–5|MAL 3:1-5*; Luke 7:24–35|LUK 7:24-35*)
units.rightText: And blessed is he, whosoever shall find no occasion of stumbling in me.
leftNotes: 11:6 Or who is not offended by Me

units.leftText: As John’s disciples were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
units.rightText: And as these went their way, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to behold? a reed shaken with the wind?

units.leftText: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings’ palaces.
units.rightText: But what went ye out to see? a man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they that wear soft raiment are in kings’ houses.

units.leftText: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
units.rightText: But wherefore went ye out? to see a prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.

units.leftText: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’
units.rightText: This is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, Who shall prepare thy way before thee.
leftNotes: 11:10 Malachi 3:1|MAL 3:1*

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not arisen a greater than John the Baptist: yet he that is but little in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

units.leftText: From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been subject to violence, and the violent lay claim to it.
units.rightText: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and men of violence take it by force.
leftNotes: 11:12 Or has been forcefully advancing

units.leftText: For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John.
units.rightText: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

units.leftText: And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come.
units.rightText: And if ye are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, that is to come.
leftNotes: 11:14 See Malachi 4:5|MAL 4:5*.

units.leftText: He who has ears, let him hear.
units.rightText: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
leftNotes: 11:15 BYZ and TR ears to hear

units.leftText: To what can I compare this generation? They are like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling out to others:
units.rightText: But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the marketplaces, who call unto their fellows

units.leftText: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn.’
units.rightText: and say, We piped unto you, and ye did not dance; we wailed, and ye did not mourn.

units.leftText: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon!’
units.rightText: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a demon.

units.leftText: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is vindicated by her actions.” Woe to the Unrepentant (Luke 10:13–16|LUK 10:13-16*)
units.rightText: The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold, a gluttonous man and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners! And wisdom is justified by her works.

units.leftText: Then Jesus began to denounce the cities in which most of His miracles had been performed, because they did not repent.
units.rightText: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not.

units.leftText: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
units.rightText: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

units.leftText: But I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
units.rightText: But I say unto you, it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the day of judgment, than for you.

units.leftText: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.
units.rightText: And thou, Capernaum, shalt thou be exalted unto heaven? thou shalt go down unto Hades: for if the mighty works had been done in Sodom which were done in thee, it would have remained until this day.

units.leftText: But I tell you that it will be more bearable for Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.” Rest for the Weary (Luke 10:21–24|LUK 10:21-24*)
units.rightText: But I say unto you that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.

units.leftText: At that time Jesus declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.
units.rightText: At that season Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou didst hide these things from the wise and understanding, and didst reveal them unto babes:

units.leftText: Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
units.rightText: yea, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in thy sight.

units.leftText: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.
units.rightText: All things have been delivered unto me of my Father: and no one knoweth the Son, save the Father; neither doth any know the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son willeth to reveal him.

units.leftText: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
units.rightText: Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

units.leftText: Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
units.rightText: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

units.leftText: For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”
units.rightText: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

units.leftText: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began to pick the heads of grain and eat them.
units.rightText: At that season Jesus went on the sabbath day through the grainfields; and his disciples were hungry and began to pluck ears and to eat.

units.leftText: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to Him, “Look, Your disciples are doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath.”
units.rightText: But the Pharisees, when they saw it, said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which it is not lawful to do upon the sabbath.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
units.rightText: But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was hungry, and they that were with him;

units.leftText: He entered the house of God, and he and his companions ate the consecrated bread, which was not lawful for them to eat, but only for the priests.
units.rightText: how he entered into the house of God, and ate the showbread, which it was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them that were with him, but only for the priests?
leftNotes: 12:4 Or the Bread of the Presence

units.leftText: Or haven’t you read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and yet are innocent?
units.rightText: Or have ye not read in the law, that on the sabbath day the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are guiltless?

units.leftText: But I tell you that One greater than the temple is here.
units.rightText: But I say unto you, that one greater than the temple is here.

units.leftText: If only you had known the meaning of ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the innocent.
units.rightText: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I desire mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
leftNotes: 12:7 Hosea 6:6|HOS 6:6*

units.leftText: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.” Jesus Heals on the Sabbath (Mark 3:1–6|MRK 3:1-6*; Luke 6:6–11|LUK 6:6-11*)
units.rightText: For the Son of man is lord of the sabbath.

units.leftText: Moving on from there, Jesus entered their synagogue,
units.rightText: And he departed thence, and went into their synagogue:

units.leftText: and a man with a withered hand was there. In order to accuse Jesus, they asked Him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
units.rightText: and behold, a man having a withered hand. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day? that they might accuse him.

units.leftText: He replied, “If one of you has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will he not take hold of it and lift it out?
units.rightText: And he said unto them, What man shall there be of you, that shall have one sheep, and if this fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?

units.leftText: How much more valuable is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”
units.rightText: How much then is a man of more value than a sheep! Wherefore it is lawful to do good on the sabbath day.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored to full use, just like the other.
units.rightText: Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, as the other.

units.leftText: But the Pharisees went out and plotted how they might kill Jesus. God’s Chosen Servant (Isaiah 42:1–9|ISA 42:1-9*)
units.rightText: But the Pharisees went out, and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.

units.leftText: Aware of this, Jesus withdrew from that place. Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them all,
units.rightText: And Jesus perceiving it withdrew from thence: and many followed him; and he healed them all,

units.leftText: warning them not to make Him known.
units.rightText: and charged them that they should not make him known:

units.leftText: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:
units.rightText: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,

units.leftText: “Here is My Servant, whom I have chosen, My beloved, in whom My soul delights. I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will proclaim justice to the nations.
units.rightText: Behold, my servant whom I have chosen; My beloved in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my Spirit upon him, And he shall declare judgment to the Gentiles.

units.leftText: He will not quarrel or cry out; no one will hear His voice in the streets.
units.rightText: He shall not strive, nor cry aloud; Neither shall any one hear his voice in the streets.

units.leftText: A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish, till He leads justice to victory.
units.rightText: A bruised reed shall he not break, And smoking flax shall he not quench, Till he send forth judgment unto victory.

units.leftText: In His name the nations will put their hope.” A House Divided (Mark 3:20–27|MRK 3:20-27*; Luke 11:14–23|LUK 11:14-23*)
units.rightText: And in his name shall the Gentiles hope.
leftNotes: 12:21 Isaiah 42:1–4|ISA 42:1-4* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to Jesus, and He healed the man so that he could speak and see.
units.rightText: Then was brought unto him one possessed with a demon, blind and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the dumb man spake and saw.

units.leftText: The crowds were astounded and asked, “Could this be the Son of David?”
units.rightText: And all the multitudes were amazed, and said, Can this be the son of David?

units.leftText: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “Only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, does this man drive out demons.”
units.rightText: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This man doth not cast out demons, but by Beelzebub the prince of the demons.
leftNotes: 12:24 WH Beezeboul; Vulgate Beelzebub; also in verse 27

units.leftText: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and every city or household divided against itself will not stand.
units.rightText: And knowing their thoughts he said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand:

units.leftText: If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then can his kingdom stand?
units.rightText: and if Satan casteth out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then shall his kingdom stand?

units.leftText: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.
units.rightText: And if I by Beelzebub cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.

units.leftText: But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
units.rightText: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then is the kingdom of God come upon you.

units.leftText: Or again, how can anyone enter a strong man’s house and steal his possessions, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can plunder his house.
units.rightText: Or how can one enter into the house of the strong man, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.

units.leftText: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters. The Unpardonable Sin (Mark 3:28–30|MRK 3:28-30*)
units.rightText: He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

units.leftText: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
units.rightText: Therefore I say unto you, Every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men; but the blasphemy against the Spirit shall not be forgiven.

units.leftText: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come. Good and Bad Fruit (Luke 6:43–45|LUK 6:43-45*)
units.rightText: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him; but whosoever shall speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, nor in that which is to come.

units.leftText: Make a tree good and its fruit will be good, or make a tree bad and its fruit will be bad, for a tree is known by its fruit.
units.rightText: Either make the tree good, and its fruit good; or make the tree corrupt, and its fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by its fruit.

units.leftText: You brood of vipers, how can you who are evil say anything good? For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.
units.rightText: Ye offspring of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

units.leftText: The good man brings good things out of his good store of treasure, and the evil man brings evil things out of his evil store of treasure.
units.rightText: The good man out of his good treasure bringeth forth good things: and the evil man out of his evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.

units.leftText: But I tell you that men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken.
units.rightText: And I say unto you, that every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.

units.leftText: For by your words you will be acquitted, and by your words you will be condemned.” The Sign of Jonah (Jonah 3:1–10|JON 3:1-10*; Luke 11:29–32|LUK 11:29-32*)
units.rightText: For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.

units.leftText: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees said to Him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.”
units.rightText: Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying, Teacher, we would see a sign from thee.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
units.rightText: But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet:

units.leftText: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
units.rightText: for as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

units.leftText: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.
units.rightText: The men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, a greater than Jonah is here.

units.leftText: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here. An Unclean Spirit Returns (Luke 11:24–26|LUK 11:24-26*)
units.rightText: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

units.leftText: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it.
units.rightText: But the unclean spirit, when he is gone out of the man, passeth through waterless places, seeking rest, and findeth it not.

units.leftText: Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’ On its return, it finds the house vacant, swept clean, and put in order.
units.rightText: Then he saith, I will return into my house whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.

units.leftText: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first. So will it be with this wicked generation.” Jesus’ Mother and Brothers (Mark 3:31–35|MRK 3:31-35*; Luke 8:19–21|LUK 8:19-21*)
units.rightText: Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man becometh worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this evil generation.

units.leftText: While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, His mother and brothers stood outside, wanting to speak to Him.
units.rightText: While he was yet speaking to the multitudes, behold, his mother and his brethren stood without, seeking to speak to him.

units.leftText: Someone told Him, “Look, Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak to You.”
units.rightText: And one said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren stand without, seeking to speak to thee.
leftNotes: 12:47 WH does not include verse 47.

units.leftText: But Jesus replied, “Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?”
units.rightText: But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?

units.leftText: Pointing to His disciples, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers.
units.rightText: And he stretched forth his hand towards his disciples, and said, Behold, my mother and my brethren!

units.leftText: For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.”
units.rightText: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.

units.leftText: That same day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the sea.
units.rightText: On that day went Jesus out of the house, and sat by the sea side.

units.leftText: Such large crowds gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat down, while all the people stood on the shore.
units.rightText: And there were gathered unto him great multitudes, so that he entered into a boat, and sat; and all the multitude stood on the beach.

units.leftText: And He told them many things in parables, saying, “A farmer went out to sow his seed.
units.rightText: And he spake to them many things in parables, saying, Behold, the sower went forth to sow;

units.leftText: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.
units.rightText: and as he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the birds came and devoured them:

units.leftText: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.
units.rightText: and others fell upon the rocky places, where they had not much earth: and straightway they sprang up, because they had no deepness of earth:

units.leftText: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.
units.rightText: and when the sun was risen, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.

units.leftText: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings.
units.rightText: And others fell upon the thorns; and the thorns grew up and choked them:

units.leftText: Still other seed fell on good soil and produced a crop — a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.
units.rightText: and others fell upon the good ground, and yielded fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

units.leftText: He who has ears, let him hear.” The Purpose of Jesus’ Parables (Isaiah 6:1–13|ISA 6:1-13*; Mark 4:10–12|MRK 4:10-12*; Luke 8:9–10|LUK 8:9-10*)
units.rightText: He that hath ears, let him hear.
leftNotes: 13:9 BYZ and TR ears to hear; also in verse 43

units.leftText: Then the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why do You speak to the people in parables?”
units.rightText: And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?

units.leftText: He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them.
units.rightText: And he answered and said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.

units.leftText: Whoever has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. Whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
units.rightText: For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that which he hath.

units.leftText: This is why I speak to them in parables: ‘Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they do not hear or understand.’
units.rightText: Therefore speak I to them in parables; because seeing they see not, and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.
leftNotes: 13:13 See Deuteronomy 29:4|DEU 29:4*, Isaiah 42:20, Jeremiah 5:21, and Ezekiel 12:2.

units.leftText: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled: ‘You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.
units.rightText: And unto them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall in no wise understand; And seeing ye shall see, and shall in no wise perceive:

units.leftText: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’
units.rightText: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, And their ears are dull of hearing, And their eyes they have closed; Lest haply they should perceive with their eyes, And hear with their ears, And understand with their heart, And should turn again, And I should heal them.
leftNotes: 13:15 Isaiah 6:9–10|ISA 6:9-10* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: But blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.
units.rightText: But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.

units.leftText: For truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous men longed to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it. The Parable of the Sower Explained (Mark 4:13–20|MRK 4:13-20*; Luke 8:11–15|LUK 8:11-15*)
units.rightText: For verily I say unto you, that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things which ye see, and saw them not; and to hear the things which ye hear, and heard them not.

units.leftText: Consider, then, the parable of the sower:
units.rightText: Hear then ye the parable of the sower.

units.leftText: When anyone hears the message of the kingdom but does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the seed sown along the path.
units.rightText: When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the evil one, and snatcheth away that which hath been sown in his heart. This is he that was sown by the way side.
leftNotes: 13:19 Literally the one sown; also in verses 20, 22, and 23

units.leftText: The seed sown on rocky ground is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.
units.rightText: And he that was sown upon the rocky places, this is he that heareth the word, and straightway with joy receiveth it;

units.leftText: But since he has no root, he remains for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he quickly falls away.
units.rightText: yet hath he not root in himself, but endureth for a while; and when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, straightway he stumbleth.

units.leftText: The seed sown among the thorns is the one who hears the word, but the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
units.rightText: And he that was sown among the thorns, this is he that heareth the word; and the care of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.

units.leftText: But the seed sown on good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it. He indeed bears fruit and produces a crop — a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.” The Parable of the Weeds (Ezekiel 17:1–10|EZK 17:1-10*)
units.rightText: And he that was sown upon the good ground, this is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; who verily beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

units.leftText: Jesus put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
units.rightText: Another parable set he before them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man that sowed good seed in his field:

units.leftText: But while everyone was asleep, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and slipped away.
units.rightText: but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares also among the wheat, and went away.

units.leftText: When the wheat sprouted and bore grain, then the weeds also appeared.
units.rightText: But when the blade sprang up and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.

units.leftText: The owner’s servants came to him and said, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the weeds come from?’
units.rightText: And the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst thou not sow good seed in thy field? whence then hath it tares?

units.leftText: ‘An enemy did this,’ he replied. So the servants asked him, ‘Do you want us to go and pull them up?’
units.rightText: And he said unto them, An enemy hath done this. And the servants say unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?

units.leftText: ‘No,’ he said, ‘if you pull the weeds now, you might uproot the wheat with them.
units.rightText: But he saith, Nay; lest haply while ye gather up the tares, ye root up the wheat with them.

units.leftText: Let both grow together until the harvest. At that time I will tell the harvesters: First collect the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned; then gather the wheat into my barn.’” The Parable of the Mustard Seed (Mark 4:30–34|MRK 4:30-34*; Luke 13:18–19|LUK 13:18-19*)
units.rightText: Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather up first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.

units.leftText: He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.
units.rightText: Another parable set he before them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like unto a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:

units.leftText: Although it is the smallest of all seeds, yet it grows into the largest of garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.” The Parable of the Leaven (Luke 13:20–21|LUK 13:20-21*)
units.rightText: which indeed is less than all seeds; but when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the heaven come and lodge in the branches thereof.

units.leftText: He told them still another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.” I Will Open My Mouth in Parables (Psalm 78:1–72|PSA 78:1-72*)
units.rightText: Another parable spake he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till it was all leavened.

units.leftText: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables. He did not tell them anything without using a parable.
units.rightText: All these things spake Jesus in parables unto the multitudes; and without a parable spake he nothing unto them:

units.leftText: So was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet: “I will open My mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden since the foundation of the world.” The Parable of the Weeds Explained (Zephaniah 1:1–6|ZEP 1:1-6*)
units.rightText: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.
leftNotes: 13:35 Psalm 78:2|PSA 78:2* (see also LXX); SBL, NE, and WH do not include of the world.

units.leftText: Then Jesus dismissed the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to Him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”
units.rightText: Then he left the multitudes, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Explain unto us the parable of the tares of the field.

units.leftText: He replied, “The One who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.
units.rightText: And he answered and said, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man;

units.leftText: The field is the world, and the good seed represents the sons of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one,
units.rightText: and the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; and the tares are the sons of the evil one;

units.leftText: and the enemy who sows them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the harvesters are angels.
units.rightText: and the enemy that sowed them is the devil: and the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are angels.

units.leftText: As the weeds are collected and burned in the fire, so will it be at the end of the age.
units.rightText: As therefore the tares are gathered up and burned with fire; so shall it be in the end of the world.

units.leftText: The Son of Man will send out His angels, and they will weed out of His kingdom every cause of sin and all who practice lawlessness.
units.rightText: The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that cause stumbling, and them that do iniquity,

units.leftText: And they will throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
units.rightText: and shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears, let him hear. The Parables of the Treasure and the Pearl
units.rightText: Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He that hath ears, let him hear.
leftNotes: 13:43 See Daniel 12:3|DAN 12:3*.

units.leftText: The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he hid it again, and in his joy he went and sold all he had and bought that field.
units.rightText: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a treasure hidden in the field; which a man found, and hid; and in his joy he goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.

units.leftText: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls.
units.rightText: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is a merchant seeking goodly pearls:

units.leftText: When he found one very precious pearl, he went away and sold all he had and bought it. The Parable of the Net
units.rightText: and having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

units.leftText: Once again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was cast into the sea and caught all kinds of fish.
units.rightText: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:

units.leftText: When it was full, the men pulled it ashore. Then they sat down and sorted the good fish into containers, but threw the bad away.
units.rightText: which, when it was filled, they drew up on the beach; and they sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but the bad they cast away.

units.leftText: So will it be at the end of the age: The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous
units.rightText: So shall it be in the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the righteous,

units.leftText: and throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
units.rightText: and shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: Have you understood all these things?” “Yes,” they answered.
units.rightText: Have ye understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea.

units.leftText: Then He told them, “For this reason, every scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old.” The Rejection at Nazareth (Mark 6:1–6|MRK 6:1-6*; Luke 4:16–30|LUK 4:16-30*)
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Therefore every scribe who hath been made a disciple to the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is a householder, who bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished these parables, He withdrew from that place.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.

units.leftText: Coming to His hometown, He taught the people in their synagogue, and they were astonished. “Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?” they asked.
units.rightText: And coming into his own country he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?

units.leftText: “Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t His mother’s name Mary, and aren’t His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
units.rightText: Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joseph, and Simon, and Judas?
leftNotes: 13:55 BYZ and TR Joses; see Mark 6:3|MRK 6:3*.

units.leftText: Aren’t all His sisters with us as well? Where then did this man get all these things?”
units.rightText: And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?

units.leftText: And they took offense at Him.
units.rightText: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honor, save in his own country, and in his own house.

units.leftText: And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief.
units.rightText: And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

units.leftText: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the reports about Jesus
units.rightText: At that season Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus,

units.leftText: and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
units.rightText: and said unto his servants, This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead; and therefore do these powers work in him.

units.leftText: Now Herod had arrested John and bound him and put him in prison on account of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife,
units.rightText: For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.

units.leftText: because John had been telling him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
units.rightText: For John said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.

units.leftText: Although Herod wanted to kill John, he was afraid of the people, because they regarded John as a prophet.
units.rightText: And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.

units.leftText: On Herod’s birthday, however, the daughter of Herodias danced before them and pleased Herod
units.rightText: But when Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst, and pleased Herod.

units.leftText: so much that he promised with an oath to give to her whatever she asked.
units.rightText: Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she should ask.

units.leftText: Prompted by her mother, she said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”
units.rightText: And she, being put forward by her mother, saith, Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.

units.leftText: The king was grieved, but because of his oaths and his guests, he ordered that her wish be granted
units.rightText: And the king was grieved; but for the sake of his oaths, and of them that sat at meat with him, he commanded it to be given;

units.leftText: and sent to have John beheaded in the prison.
units.rightText: and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.

units.leftText: John’s head was brought in on a platter and presented to the girl, who carried it to her mother.
units.rightText: And his head was brought on a platter, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.

units.leftText: Then John’s disciples came and took his body and buried it. And they went and informed Jesus. The Feeding of the Five Thousand (Mark 6:30–44|MRK 6:30-44*; Luke 9:10–17|LUK 9:10-17*; John 6:1–15|JHN 6:1-15*)
units.rightText: And his disciples came, and took up the corpse, and buried him; and they went and told Jesus.

units.leftText: When Jesus heard about John, He withdrew by boat privately to a solitary place. But the crowds found out about it and followed Him on foot from the towns.
units.rightText: Now when Jesus heard it, he withdrew from thence in a boat, to a desert place apart: and when the multitudes heard thereof, they followed him on foot from the cities.

units.leftText: When He stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them and healed their sick.
units.rightText: And he came forth, and saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them, and healed their sick.

units.leftText: When evening came, the disciples came to Him and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late. Dismiss the crowds so they can go to the villages and buy themselves some food.”
units.rightText: And when even was come, the disciples came to him, saying, The place is desert, and the time is already past; send the multitudes away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves food.

units.leftText: “They do not need to go away,” Jesus replied. “You give them something to eat.”
units.rightText: But Jesus said unto them, They have no need to go away; give ye them to eat.

units.leftText: “We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered.
units.rightText: And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes.

units.leftText: “Bring them here to Me,” Jesus said.
units.rightText: And he said, Bring them hither to me.

units.leftText: And He directed the crowds to sit down on the grass. Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, He spoke a blessing. Then He broke the loaves and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.
units.rightText: And he commanded the multitudes to sit down on the grass; and he took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake and gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.

units.leftText: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
units.rightText: And they all ate, and were filled: and they took up that which remained over of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full.

units.leftText: About five thousand men were fed, besides women and children. Jesus Walks on Water (Mark 6:45–52|MRK 6:45-52*; John 6:16–21|JHN 6:16-21*)
units.rightText: And they that did eat were about five thousand men, besides women and children.

units.leftText: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to the other side, while He dismissed the crowds.
units.rightText: And straightway he constrained the disciples to enter into the boat, and to go before him unto the other side, till he should send the multitudes away.

units.leftText: After He had dismissed them, He went up on the mountain by Himself to pray. When evening came, He was there alone,
units.rightText: And after he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into the mountain apart to pray: and when even was come, he was there alone.

units.leftText: but the boat was already far from land, buffeted by the waves because the wind was against it.
units.rightText: But the boat was now in the midst of the sea, distressed by the waves; for the wind was contrary.
leftNotes: 14:24 Greek many stadia; a stadion was about 607 feet or 185 meters

units.leftText: During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea.
units.rightText: And in the fourth watch of the night he came unto them, walking upon the sea.
leftNotes: 14:25 That is, between three and six in the morning

units.leftText: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were terrified. “It’s a ghost!” they said, and cried out in fear.
units.rightText: And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a ghost; and they cried out for fear.

units.leftText: But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
units.rightText: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

units.leftText: “Lord, if it is You,” Peter replied, “command me to come to You on the water.”
units.rightText: And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee upon the waters.

units.leftText: “Come,” said Jesus.
units.rightText: And he said, Come. And Peter went down from the boat, and walked upon the waters to come to Jesus.

units.leftText: But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid and, beginning to sink, cried out, “Lord, save me!”
units.rightText: But when he saw the wind, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, Lord, save me.
leftNotes: 14:30 Literally when he saw the strong wind; NE and WH do not include strong.

units.leftText: Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter. “You of little faith,” He said, “why did you doubt?”
units.rightText: And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and took hold of him, and saith unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?

units.leftText: And when they had climbed back into the boat, the wind died down.
units.rightText: And when they were gone up into the boat, the wind ceased.

units.leftText: Then those who were in the boat worshiped Him, saying, “Truly You are the Son of God!” Jesus Heals at Gennesaret (Mark 6:53–56|MRK 6:53-56*)
units.rightText: And they that were in the boat worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God.

units.leftText: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret.
units.rightText: And when they had crossed over, they came to the land, unto Gennesaret.

units.leftText: And when the men of that place recognized Jesus, they sent word to all the surrounding region. People brought all the sick to Him
units.rightText: And when the men of that place knew him, they sent into all that region round about, and brought unto him all that were sick;

units.leftText: and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.
units.rightText: and they besought him that they might only touch the border of his garment: and as many as touched were made whole.

units.leftText: Then some Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem and asked,
units.rightText: Then there come to Jesus from Jerusalem Pharisees and scribes, saying,

units.leftText: “Why do Your disciples break the tradition of the elders? They do not wash their hands before they eat.”
units.rightText: Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “And why do you break the command of God for the sake of your tradition?
units.rightText: And he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition?

units.leftText: For God said, ‘Honor your father and mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’
units.rightText: For God said, Honor thy father and thy mother: and, He that speaketh evil of father or mother, let him die the death.
leftNotes: 15:4 Exodus 20:12|EXO 20:12*; Deuteronomy 5:16
15:4 Exodus 21:17|EXO 21:17*; Leviticus 20:9

units.leftText: But you say that if anyone says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is a gift devoted to God,’
units.rightText: But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, That wherewith thou mightest have been profited by me is given to God;

units.leftText: he need not honor his father or mother with it. Thus you nullify the word of God for the sake of your tradition.
units.rightText: he shall not honor his father. And ye have made void the word of God because of your tradition.
leftNotes: 15:6 NE and TR (see also Mark 7:12|MRK 7:12*); literally he need not honor his father or mother; SBL, NA, WH, and BYZ do not include or mother.

units.leftText: You hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied correctly about you:
units.rightText: Ye hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,

units.leftText: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
units.rightText: This people honoreth me with their lips; But their heart is far from me.

units.leftText: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’ ” What Defiles a Man (Mark 7:14–23|MRK 7:14-23*)
units.rightText: But in vain do they worship me, Teaching as their doctrines the precepts of men.
leftNotes: 15:9 Isaiah 29:13|ISA 29:13* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “Listen and understand.
units.rightText: And he called to him the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand:

units.leftText: A man is not defiled by what enters his mouth, but by what comes out of it.”
units.rightText: Not that which entereth into the mouth defileth the man; but that which proceedeth out of the mouth, this defileth the man.

units.leftText: Then the disciples came to Him and said, “Are You aware that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?”
units.rightText: Then came the disciples, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, when they heard this saying?

units.leftText: But Jesus replied, “Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots.
units.rightText: But he answered and said, Every plant which my heavenly Father planted not, shall be rooted up.

units.leftText: Disregard them! They are blind guides. If a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit.”
units.rightText: Let them alone: they are blind guides. And if the blind guide the blind, both shall fall into a pit.
leftNotes: 15:14 Or blind guides of the blind

units.leftText: Peter said to Him, “Explain this parable to us.”
units.rightText: And Peter answered and said unto him, Declare unto us the parable.

units.leftText: “Do you still not understand?” Jesus asked.
units.rightText: And he said, Are ye also even yet without understanding?

units.leftText: “Do you not yet realize that whatever enters the mouth goes into the stomach and then is eliminated?
units.rightText: Perceive ye not, that whatsoever goeth into the mouth passeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?

units.leftText: But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these things defile a man.
units.rightText: But the things which proceed out of the mouth come forth out of the heart; and they defile the man.

units.leftText: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander.
units.rightText: For out of the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, railings:

units.leftText: These are what defile a man, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile him.” The Faith of the Canaanite Woman (Mark 7:24–30|MRK 7:24-30*)
units.rightText: these are the things which defile the man; but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not the man.

units.leftText: Leaving that place, Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon.
units.rightText: And Jesus went out thence, and withdrew into the parts of Tyre and Sidon.

units.leftText: And a Canaanite woman from that region came to Him, crying out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter is miserably possessed by a demon.”
units.rightText: And behold, a Canaanitish woman came out from those borders, and cried, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a demon.

units.leftText: But Jesus did not answer a word. So His disciples came and urged Him, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.”
units.rightText: But he answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she crieth after us.

units.leftText: He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
units.rightText: But he answered and said, I was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

units.leftText: The woman came and knelt before Him. “Lord, help me!” she said.
units.rightText: But she came and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me.

units.leftText: But Jesus replied, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
units.rightText: And he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread and cast it to the dogs.

units.leftText: “Yes, Lord,” she said, “even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.”
units.rightText: But she said, Yea, Lord: for even the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.
leftNotes: 15:27 Or puppies

units.leftText: “O woman,” Jesus answered, “your faith is great! Let it be done for you as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that very hour. The Feeding of the Four Thousand (2 Kings 4:42–44|2KI 4:42-44*; Mark 8:1–10|MRK 8:1-10*)
units.rightText: Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it done unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was healed from that hour.

units.leftText: Moving on from there, Jesus went along the Sea of Galilee. Then He went up on a mountain and sat down.
units.rightText: And Jesus departed thence, and came nigh unto the sea of Galilee; and he went up into the mountain, and sat there.

units.leftText: Large crowds came to Him, bringing the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others, and laid them at His feet, and He healed them.
units.rightText: And there came unto him great multitudes, having with them the lame, blind, dumb, maimed, and many others, and they cast them down at his feet; and he healed them:

units.leftText: The crowd was amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled restored, the lame walking, and the blind seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel.
units.rightText: insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb speaking, the maimed whole, and the lame walking, and the blind seeing: and they glorified the God of Israel.

units.leftText: Then Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint along the way.”
units.rightText: And Jesus called unto him his disciples, and said, I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days and have nothing to eat: and I would not send them away fasting, lest haply they faint on the way.

units.leftText: The disciples replied, “Where in this desolate place could we find enough bread to feed such a large crowd?”
units.rightText: And the disciples say unto him, Whence should we have so many loaves in a desert place as to fill so great a multitude?

units.leftText: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied, “and a few small fish.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven, and a few small fishes.

units.leftText: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground.
units.rightText: And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground;

units.leftText: Taking the seven loaves and the fish, He gave thanks and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.
units.rightText: and he took the seven loaves and the fishes; and he gave thanks and brake, and gave to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.

units.leftText: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
units.rightText: And they all ate, and were filled: and they took up that which remained over of the broken pieces, seven baskets full.

units.leftText: A total of four thousand men were fed, besides women and children.
units.rightText: And they that did eat were four thousand men, besides women and children.

units.leftText: After Jesus had dismissed the crowds, He got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.
units.rightText: And he sent away the multitudes, and entered into the boat, and came into the borders of Magadan.

units.leftText: Then the Pharisees and Sadducees came and tested Jesus by asking Him to show them a sign from heaven.
units.rightText: And the Pharisees and Sadducees came, and trying him asked him to show them a sign from heaven.

units.leftText: But He replied, “When evening comes, you say, ‘The weather will be fair, for the sky is red,’
units.rightText: But he answered and said unto them, When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the heaven is red.

units.leftText: and in the morning, ‘Today it will be stormy, for the sky is red and overcast.’ You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky, but not the signs of the times.
units.rightText: And in the morning, It will be foul weather to-day: for the heaven is red and lowering. Ye know how to discern the face of the heaven; but ye cannot discern the signs of the times.
leftNotes: 16:3 Several manuscripts do not include When evening comes... of the times. from verses 2 and 3.

units.leftText: A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.” Then He left them and went away. The Leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees (Mark 8:14–21|MRK 8:14-21*; Luke 12:1–3|LUK 12:1-3*)
units.rightText: An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given unto it, but the sign of Jonah. And he left them, and departed.

units.leftText: When they crossed to the other side, the disciples forgot to take bread.
units.rightText: And the disciples came to the other side and forgot to take bread.

units.leftText: “Watch out!” Jesus told them. “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

units.leftText: They discussed this among themselves and concluded, “It is because we did not bring any bread.”
units.rightText: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, We took no bread.

units.leftText: Aware of their conversation, Jesus said, “You of little faith, why are you debating among yourselves about having no bread?
units.rightText: And Jesus perceiving it said, O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves, because ye have no bread?

units.leftText: Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?
units.rightText: Do ye not yet perceive, neither remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?

units.leftText: Or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?
units.rightText: Neither the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?

units.leftText: How do you not understand that I was not telling you about bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
units.rightText: How is it that ye do not perceive that I spake not to you concerning bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

units.leftText: Then they understood that He was not telling them to beware of the leaven used in bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees. Peter’s Confession of Christ (Mark 8:27–30|MRK 8:27-30*; Luke 9:18–20|LUK 9:18-20*; John 6:67–71|JHN 6:67-71*)
units.rightText: Then understood they that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

units.leftText: When Jesus came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, He questioned His disciples: “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”
units.rightText: Now when Jesus came into the parts of Cæsarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Who do men say that the Son of man is?

units.leftText: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
units.rightText: And they said, Some say John the Baptist; some, Elijah; and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.

units.leftText: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?”
units.rightText: He saith unto them, But who say ye that I am?

units.leftText: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
units.rightText: And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! For this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-Jonah: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father who is in heaven.
leftNotes: 16:17 Greek Simon Bar-Jonah

units.leftText: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
units.rightText: And I also say unto thee, that thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.

units.leftText: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.”
units.rightText: I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

units.leftText: Then He admonished the disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ. Christ’s Passion Foretold (Mark 8:31–33|MRK 8:31-33*; Luke 9:21–22|LUK 9:21-22*)
units.rightText: Then charged he the disciples that they should tell no man that he was the Christ.

units.leftText: From that time on Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.
units.rightText: From that time began Jesus to show unto his disciples, that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.
leftNotes: 16:21 NE and WH Jesus Christ

units.leftText: Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him. “Far be it from You, Lord!” he said. “This shall never happen to You!”
units.rightText: And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall never be unto thee.

units.leftText: But Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me. For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.” Take Up Your Cross (Mark 8:34–38|MRK 8:34-38*; Luke 9:23–27|LUK 9:23-27*)
units.rightText: But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art a stumbling-block unto me: for thou mindest not the things of God, but the things of men.

units.leftText: Then Jesus told His disciples, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
units.rightText: Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man would come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

units.leftText: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.
units.rightText: For whosoever would save his life shall lose it: and whosoever shall lose his life for my sake shall find it.

units.leftText: What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
units.rightText: For what shall a man be profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and forfeit his life? or what shall a man give in exchange for his life?

units.leftText: For the Son of Man will come in His Father’s glory with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to what he has done.
units.rightText: For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then shall he render unto every man according to his deeds.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.”
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, There are some of them that stand here, who shall in no wise taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.

units.leftText: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John the brother of James, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.
units.rightText: And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into a high mountain apart:

units.leftText: There He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as the light.
units.rightText: and he was transfigured before them; and his face did shine as the sun, and his garments became white as the light.

units.leftText: Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus.
units.rightText: And behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elijah talking with him.

units.leftText: Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If You wish, I will put up three shelters — one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
units.rightText: And Peter answered, and said unto Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, I will make here three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
leftNotes: 17:4 Or three tabernacles

units.leftText: While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud enveloped them, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!”
units.rightText: While he was yet speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold, a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.
leftNotes: 17:5 Cited in 2 Peter 1:17|2PE 1:17*

units.leftText: When the disciples heard this, they fell facedown in terror.
units.rightText: And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were sore afraid.

units.leftText: Then Jesus came over and touched them. “Get up,” He said. “Do not be afraid.”
units.rightText: And Jesus came and touched them and said, Arise, and be not afraid.

units.leftText: And when they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
units.rightText: And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one, save Jesus only.

units.leftText: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them, “Do not tell anyone about this vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.”
units.rightText: And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen from the dead.

units.leftText: The disciples asked Him, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
units.rightText: And his disciples asked him, saying, Why then say the scribes that Elijah must first come?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things.
units.rightText: And he answered and said, Elijah indeed cometh, and shall restore all things:

units.leftText: But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but have done to him whatever they wished. In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer at their hands.”
units.rightText: but I say unto you, that Elijah is come already, and they knew him not, but did unto him whatsoever they would. Even so shall the Son of man also suffer of them.

units.leftText: Then the disciples understood that He was speaking to them about John the Baptist. The Boy with a Demon (Mark 9:14–29|MRK 9:14-29*; Luke 9:37–42|LUK 9:37-42*)
units.rightText: Then understood the disciples that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.

units.leftText: When they came to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus and knelt before Him.
units.rightText: And when they were come to the multitude, there came to him a man, kneeling to him, and saying,

units.leftText: “Lord, have mercy on my son,” he said. “He has seizures and is suffering terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.
units.rightText: Lord, have mercy on my son: for he is epileptic, and suffereth grievously; for oft-times he falleth into the fire, and oft-times into the water.

units.leftText: I brought him to Your disciples, but they could not heal him.”
units.rightText: And I brought him to thy disciples, and they could not cure him.

units.leftText: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to Me.”
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I bear with you? bring him hither to me.

units.leftText: Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, and he was healed from that moment. The Power of Faith (Luke 17:5–10|LUK 17:5-10*)
units.rightText: And Jesus rebuked him; and the demon went out of him: and the boy was cured from that hour.

units.leftText: Afterward the disciples came to Jesus privately and asked, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
units.rightText: Then came the disciples to Jesus apart, and said, Why could not we cast it out?
