units.leftText: “Because you have so little faith,” He answered. “For truly I tell you, if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.” The Second Prediction of the Passion (Mark 9:30–32|MRK 9:30-32*; Luke 9:43–45|LUK 9:43-45*)
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Because of your little faith: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.
leftNotes: 17:20 BYZ and TR include 21*But this kind does not come out except by prayer and fasting; see Mark 9:29|MRK 9:29*.

rightNotes: 17:21 Many authorities, some ancient, insert v. 21. But this kind goeth not out save by prayer and fasting. See Mrk 9:29.

units.leftText: When they gathered together in Galilee, Jesus told them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.
units.rightText: And while they abode in Galilee, Jesus said unto them, The Son of man shall be delivered up into the hands of men;

units.leftText: They will kill Him, and on the third day He will be raised to life.” And the disciples were deeply grieved. The Temple Tax
units.rightText: and they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised up. And they were exceeding sorry.

units.leftText: After they had arrived in Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and asked, “Does your Teacher pay the two drachmas?”
units.rightText: And when they were come to Capernaum, they that received the half-shekel came to Peter, and said, Doth not your teacher pay the half-shekel?
leftNotes: 17:24 Greek the didrachma; twice in this verse

units.leftText: “Yes,” he answered. When Peter entered the house, Jesus preempted him. “What do you think, Simon?” He asked. “From whom do the kings of the earth collect customs and taxes: from their own sons, or from others?”
units.rightText: He saith, Yea. And when he came into the house, Jesus spake first to him, saying, What thinkest thou, Simon? the kings of the earth, from whom do they receive toll or tribute? from their sons, or from strangers?

units.leftText: “From others,” Peter answered.
units.rightText: And when he said, From strangers, Jesus said unto him, Therefore the sons are free.

units.leftText: “But so that we may not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a four-drachma coin. Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.”
units.rightText: But, lest we cause them to stumble, go thou to the sea, and cast a hook, and take up the fish that first cometh up; and when thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a shekel: that take, and give unto them for me and thee.
leftNotes: 17:27 Greek a stater; that is, a silver coin worth approximately one shekel

units.leftText: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
units.rightText: In that hour came the disciples unto Jesus, saying, Who then is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?

units.leftText: Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.
units.rightText: And he called to him a little child, and set him in the midst of them,

units.leftText: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
units.rightText: and said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye turn, and become as little children, ye shall in no wise enter into the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
units.rightText: Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me. Temptations and Trespasses (Mark 9:42–48|MRK 9:42-48*; Luke 17:1–4|LUK 17:1-4*)
units.rightText: And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me:

units.leftText: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
units.rightText: but whoso shall cause one of these little ones that believe on me to stumble, it is profitable for him that a great millstone should be hanged about his neck, and that he should be sunk in the depth of the sea.

units.leftText: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!
units.rightText: Woe unto the world because of occasions of stumbling! for it must needs be that the occasions come; but woe to that man through whom the occasion cometh!

units.leftText: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
units.rightText: And if thy hand or thy foot causeth thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee to enter into life maimed or halt, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.

units.leftText: And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell. The Parable of the Lost Sheep (Luke 15:1–7|LUK 15:1-7*)
units.rightText: And if thine eye causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the hell of fire.
leftNotes: 18:9 Or the hell of fire; Greek the Gehenna of fire

units.leftText: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.
units.rightText: See that ye despise not one of these little ones: for I say unto you, that in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father who is in heaven.
leftNotes: 18:10 BYZ and TR include 11*For the Son of Man came to save the lost; see Luke 19:10|LUK 19:10*.

rightNotes: 18:11 Many authorities, some ancient, insert v. 11. For the son of man came to save that which was lost. See Luk 19:10.

units.leftText: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?
units.rightText: How think ye? if any man have a hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and go unto the mountains, and seek that which goeth astray?

units.leftText: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
units.rightText: And if so be that he find it, verily I say unto you, he rejoiceth over it more than over the ninety and nine which have not gone astray.

units.leftText: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish. A Brother Who Sins (Deuteronomy 19:15–21|DEU 19:15-21*)
units.rightText: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.

units.leftText: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.
units.rightText: And if thy brother sin against thee, go, show him his fault between thee and him alone: if he hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.
leftNotes: 18:15 NE and WH do not include against you.

units.leftText: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
units.rightText: But if he hear thee not, take with thee one or two more, that at the mouth of two witnesses or three every word may be established.
leftNotes: 18:16 Deuteronomy 19:15|DEU 19:15*

units.leftText: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.
units.rightText: And if he refuse to hear them, tell it unto the church: and if he refuse to hear the church also, let him be unto thee as the Gentile and the publican.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven. Ask in My Name (John 16:23–33|JHN 16:23-33*)
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, What things soever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and what things soever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

units.leftText: Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.
units.rightText: Again I say unto you, that if two of you shall agree on earth as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father who is in heaven.

units.leftText: For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.” The Unforgiving Servant (Romans 12:14–21|ROM 12:14-21*)
units.rightText: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.

units.leftText: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”
units.rightText: Then came Peter and said to him, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? until seven times?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times; but, Until seventy times seven.
leftNotes: 18:22 Or seventy times seven; see Genesis 4:24|GEN 4:24* LXX

units.leftText: Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
units.rightText: Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, who would make a reckoning with his servants.

units.leftText: As he began the settlements, a debtor owing ten thousand talents was brought to him.
units.rightText: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, that owed him ten thousand talents.
leftNotes: 18:24 A talent was worth about twenty years’ wages for a laborer.

units.leftText: Since the man was unable to pay, the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt, along with his wife and children and everything he owned.
units.rightText: But forasmuch as he had not wherewith to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.

units.leftText: Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’
units.rightText: The servant therefore fell down and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.

units.leftText: His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.
units.rightText: And the lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt.

units.leftText: But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe me!’
units.rightText: But that servant went out, and found one of his fellow-servants, who owed him a hundred shillings: and he laid hold on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay what thou owest.
leftNotes: 18:28 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: So his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.’
units.rightText: So his fellow-servant fell down and besought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay thee.

units.leftText: But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay his debt.
units.rightText: And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay that which was due.

units.leftText: When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and recounted all of this to their master.
units.rightText: So when his fellow-servants saw what was done, they were exceeding sorry, and came and told unto their lord all that was done.

units.leftText: Then the master summoned him and said, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me.
units.rightText: Then his lord called him unto him, and saith to him, Thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou besoughtest me:

units.leftText: Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?’
units.rightText: shouldest not thou also have had mercy on thy fellow-servant, even as I had mercy on thee?

units.leftText: In anger his master turned him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should repay all that he owed.
units.rightText: And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due.

units.leftText: That is how My heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother from your heart.”
units.rightText: So shall also my heavenly Father do unto you, if ye forgive not every one his brother from your hearts.

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished saying these things, He left Galilee and went into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.
units.rightText: And it came to pass when Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee, and came into the borders of Judæa beyond the Jordan;

units.leftText: Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them there.
units.rightText: and great multitudes followed him; and he healed them there.

units.leftText: Then some Pharisees came and tested Him by asking, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”
units.rightText: And there came unto him Pharisees, trying him, and saying, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’
units.rightText: And he answered and said, Have ye not read, that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female,
leftNotes: 19:4 Genesis 1:27|GEN 1:27*; Genesis 5:2

units.leftText: and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’ ?
units.rightText: and said, For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh?
leftNotes: 19:5 Genesis 2:24|GEN 2:24* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”
units.rightText: So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

units.leftText: “Why then,” they asked, “did Moses order a man to give his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away? ”
units.rightText: They say unto him, Why then did Moses command to give a bill of divorcement, and to put her away?
leftNotes: 19:7 See Deuteronomy 24:1|DEU 24:1*.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because of your hardness of heart. But it was not this way from the beginning.
units.rightText: He saith unto them, Moses for your hardness of heart suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it hath not been so.

units.leftText: Now I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman commits adultery. ”
units.rightText: And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and he that marrieth her when she is put away committeth adultery.
leftNotes: 19:9 SBL and BYZ include And he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery; see Matthew 5:32|MAT 5:32*.

units.leftText: His disciples said to Him, “If this is the case between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry.”
units.rightText: The disciples say unto him, If the case of the man is so with his wife, it is not expedient to marry.

units.leftText: “Not everyone can accept this word,” He replied, “but only those to whom it has been given.
units.rightText: But he said unto them, Not all men can receive this saying, but they to whom it is given.

units.leftText: For there are eunuchs who were born that way; others were made that way by men; and still others live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who can accept this should accept it.” Jesus Blesses the Children (Mark 10:13–16|MRK 10:13-16*; Luke 18:15–17|LUK 18:15-17*)
units.rightText: For there are eunuchs, that were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are eunuchs, that were made eunuchs by men: and there are eunuchs, that made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven’s sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.

units.leftText: Then little children were brought to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them and pray for them. And the disciples rebuked those who brought them.
units.rightText: Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should lay his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them.

units.leftText: But Jesus said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”
units.rightText: But Jesus said, Suffer the little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for to such belongeth the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: And after He had placed His hands on them, He went on from there. The Rich Young Man (Mark 10:17–31|MRK 10:17-31*; Luke 18:18–30|LUK 18:18-30*)
units.rightText: And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.

units.leftText: Just then a man came up to Jesus and inquired, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?”
units.rightText: And behold, one came to him and said, Teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?

units.leftText: “Why do you ask Me about what is good?” Jesus replied. “There is only One who is good. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Why askest thou me concerning that which is good? One there is who is good: but if thou wouldest enter into life, keep the commandments.
leftNotes: 19:17 BYZ and TR 16*...“Good Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?” 17*“Why do you call Me good?”See Mark 10:17–18|MRK 10:17-18* and Luke 18:18–19.

units.leftText: “Which ones?” the man asked.
units.rightText: He saith unto him, Which? And Jesus said, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness,

units.leftText: honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
units.rightText: Honor thy father and thy mother; and, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
leftNotes: 19:19 Exodus 20:12–16|EXO 20:12-16*; Leviticus 19:18; Deuteronomy 5:16–20

units.leftText: “All these I have kept,” said the young man. “What do I still lack?”
units.rightText: The young man saith unto him, All these things have I observed: what lack I yet?

units.leftText: Jesus told him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
units.rightText: Jesus said unto him, If thou wouldest be perfect, go, sell that which thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.

units.leftText: When the young man heard this, he went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.
units.rightText: But when the young man heard the saying, he went away sorrowful; for he was one that had great possessions.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Truly I tell you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, It is hard for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
units.rightText: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and asked, “Who then can be saved?”
units.rightText: And when the disciples heard it, they were astonished exceedingly, saying, Who then can be saved?

units.leftText: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
units.rightText: And Jesus looking upon them said to them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.

units.leftText: “Look,” Peter replied, “we have left everything to follow You. What then will there be for us?”
units.rightText: Then answered Peter and said unto him, Lo, we have left all, and followed thee; what then shall we have?

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, in the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, Verily I say unto you, that ye who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit on the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
leftNotes: 19:28 Or in the regeneration

units.leftText: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of My name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.
units.rightText: And every one that hath left houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, shall receive a hundredfold, and shall inherit eternal life.
leftNotes: 19:29 NE, WH, and NA do not include or wife.

units.leftText: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.[’’]
units.rightText: But many shall be last that are first; and first that are last.

units.leftText: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
units.rightText: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that was a householder, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers into his vineyard.

units.leftText: He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.
units.rightText: And when he had agreed with the laborers for a shilling a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
leftNotes: 20:2 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; similarly in verses 9, 10, and 13.

units.leftText: About the third hour he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.
units.rightText: And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing in the marketplace idle;
leftNotes: 20:3 That is, about nine in the morning

units.leftText: ‘You also go into my vineyard,’ he said, ‘and I will pay you whatever is right.’
units.rightText: and to them he said, Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way.

units.leftText: So they went. He went out again about the sixth hour and the ninth hour and did the same thing.
units.rightText: Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did likewise.
leftNotes: 20:5 That is, about noon and again about three in the afternoon

units.leftText: About the eleventh hour he went out and found still others standing around. ‘Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?’ he asked.
units.rightText: And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing; and he saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?
leftNotes: 20:6 That is, about five in the afternoon; also in verse 9

units.leftText: ‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered. So he told them, ‘You also go into my vineyard.’
units.rightText: They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard.
leftNotes: 20:7 BYZ and TR include and whatever is right, you shall receive.

units.leftText: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first.’
units.rightText: And when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the laborers, and pay them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.

units.leftText: The workers who were hired about the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.
units.rightText: And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a shilling.

units.leftText: So when the original workers came, they assumed they would receive more. But each of them also received a denarius.
units.rightText: And when the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise received every man a shilling.

units.leftText: On receiving their pay, they began to grumble against the landowner.
units.rightText: And when they received it, they murmured against the householder,

units.leftText: ‘These men who were hired last worked only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden and the scorching heat of the day.’
units.rightText: saying, These last have spent but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.

units.leftText: But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am not being unfair to you. Did you not agree with me on one denarius?
units.rightText: But he answered and said to one of them, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a shilling?

units.leftText: Take your pay and go. I want to give this last man the same as I gave you.
units.rightText: Take up that which is thine, and go thy way; it is my will to give unto this last, even as unto thee.

units.leftText: Do I not have the right to do as I please with what is mine? Or are you envious because I am generous?’
units.rightText: Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? or is thine eye evil, because I am good?

units.leftText: So the last will be first, and the first will be last.” The Third Prediction of the Passion (Mark 10:32–34|MRK 10:32-34*; Luke 18:31–34|LUK 18:31-34*)
units.rightText: So the last shall be first, and the first last.
leftNotes: 20:16 BYZ and TR include For many are called, but few are chosen.

units.leftText: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples aside and said,
units.rightText: And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples apart, and on the way he said unto them,

units.leftText: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death
units.rightText: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests and scribes; and they shall condemn him to death,

units.leftText: and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified. And on the third day He will be raised to life.” A Mother’s Request (Mark 10:35–45|MRK 10:35-45*)
units.rightText: and shall deliver him unto the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify: and the third day he shall be raised up.

units.leftText: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and knelt down to make a request of Him.
units.rightText: Then came to him the mother of the sons of Zebedee with her sons, worshipping him, and asking a certain thing of him.

units.leftText: “What do you want?” He inquired. She answered, “Declare that in Your kingdom one of these two sons of mine may sit at Your right hand, and the other at Your left.”
units.rightText: And he said unto her, What wouldest thou? She saith unto him, Command that these my two sons may sit, one on thy right hand, and one on thy left hand, in thy kingdom.

units.leftText: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?” “We can,” the brothers answered.
units.rightText: But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? They say unto him, We are able.
leftNotes: 20:22 BYZ includes or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized. TR is similar.

units.leftText: “You will indeed drink My cup,” Jesus said. “But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them.”
units.rightText: He saith unto them, My cup indeed ye shall drink: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left hand, is not mine to give; but it is for them for whom it hath been prepared of my Father.
leftNotes: 20:23 BYZ and TR include and be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.

units.leftText: When the ten heard about this, they were indignant with the two brothers.
units.rightText: And when the ten heard it, they were moved with indignation concerning the two brethren.

units.leftText: But Jesus called them aside and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.
units.rightText: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

units.leftText: It shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,
units.rightText: Not so shall it be among you: but whosoever would become great among you shall be your minister;

units.leftText: and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave —
units.rightText: and whosoever would be first among you shall be your servant:

units.leftText: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.” The Blind Men by the Road (Mark 10:46–52|MRK 10:46-52*; Luke 18:35–43|LUK 18:35-43*)
units.rightText: even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

units.leftText: As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed Him.
units.rightText: And as they went out from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.

units.leftText: And there were two blind men sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
units.rightText: And behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying, Lord, have mercy on us, thou son of David.

units.leftText: The crowd admonished them to be silent, but they cried out all the louder, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
units.rightText: And the multitude rebuked them, that they should hold their peace: but they cried out the more, saying, Lord, have mercy on us, thou son of David.

units.leftText: Jesus stopped and called them. “What do you want Me to do for you?” He asked.
units.rightText: And Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, What will ye that I should do unto you?

units.leftText: “Lord,” they answered, “let our eyes be opened.”
units.rightText: They say unto him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened.

units.leftText: Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and at once they received their sight and followed Him.
units.rightText: And Jesus, being moved with compassion, touched their eyes; and straightway they received their sight, and followed him.

units.leftText: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two disciples,
units.rightText: And when they drew nigh unto Jerusalem, and came unto Bethphage, unto the mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,

units.leftText: saying to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to Me.
units.rightText: saying unto them, Go into the village that is over against you, and straightway ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me.

units.leftText: If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.”
units.rightText: And if any one say aught unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and straightway he will send them.

units.leftText: This took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet:
units.rightText: Now this is come to pass, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,

units.leftText: “Say to the Daughter of Zion, ‘See, your King comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’”
units.rightText: Tell ye the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, Meek, and riding upon an ass, And upon a colt the foal of an ass.
leftNotes: 21:5 Zechariah 9:9|ZEC 9:9*

units.leftText: So the disciples went and did as Jesus had directed them.
units.rightText: And the disciples went, and did even as Jesus appointed them,

units.leftText: They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.
units.rightText: and brought the ass, and the colt, and put on them their garments; and he sat thereon.

units.leftText: A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
units.rightText: And the most part of the multitude spread their garments in the way; and others cut branches from the trees, and spread them in the way.

units.leftText: The crowds that went ahead of Him and those that followed were shouting: “Hosanna to the Son of David!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Hosanna in the highest!”
units.rightText: And the multitudes that went before him, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.
leftNotes: 21:9 Hosanna is a transliteration of the Hebrew Hosia-na, meaning Save, we pray or Save now, which became a shout of praise; see Psalm 118:25|PSA 118:25*; also in verse 15.
21:9 Or “Hosanna in the highest heaven!”See Psalm 118:25|PSA 118:25* and Psalm 148:1.

units.leftText: When Jesus had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and asked, “Who is this?”
units.rightText: And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred, saying, Who is this?

units.leftText: The crowds replied, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.” Jesus Cleanses the Temple (Mark 11:15–19|MRK 11:15-19*; Luke 19:45–48|LUK 19:45-48*; John 2:12–25|JHN 2:12-25*)
units.rightText: And the multitudes said, This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.

units.leftText: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
units.rightText: And Jesus entered into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers, and the seats of them that sold the doves;
leftNotes: 21:12 Literally the temple; also in verses 15 and 23; BYZ and TR the temple of God

units.leftText: And He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’ But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’ ”
units.rightText: and he saith unto them, It is written, My house shall be called a house of prayer: but ye make it a den of robbers.
leftNotes: 21:13 Jeremiah 7:11|JER 7:11*

units.leftText: The blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them.
units.rightText: And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple; and he healed them.

units.leftText: But the chief priests and scribes were indignant when they saw the wonders He performed and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”
units.rightText: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children that were crying in the temple and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were moved with indignation,

units.leftText: “Do You hear what these children are saying?” they asked. “Yes,” Jesus answered. “Have you never read: ‘From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise’ ?”
units.rightText: and said unto him, Hearest thou what these are saying? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea: did ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?
leftNotes: 21:16 Psalm 8:2|PSA 8:2* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Then He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where He spent the night. The Barren Fig Tree (Mark 11:12–14|MRK 11:12-14*; Mark 11:20–25|MRK 11:20-25*)
units.rightText: And he left them, and went forth out of the city to Bethany, and lodged there.

units.leftText: In the morning, as Jesus was returning to the city, He was hungry.
units.rightText: Now in the morning as he returned to the city, he hungered.

units.leftText: Seeing a fig tree by the road, He went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. “May you never bear fruit again!” He said. And immediately the tree withered.
units.rightText: And seeing a fig tree by the way side, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only; and he saith unto it, Let there be no fruit from thee henceforward for ever. And immediately the fig tree withered away.

units.leftText: When the disciples saw this, they marveled and asked, “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?”
units.rightText: And when the disciples saw it, they marvelled, saying, How did the fig tree immediately wither away?

units.leftText: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do what is done to the fig tree, but even if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou taken up and cast into the sea, it shall be done.

units.leftText: If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.” Jesus’ Authority Challenged (Mark 11:27–33|MRK 11:27-33*; Luke 20:1–8|LUK 20:1-8*)
units.rightText: And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.

units.leftText: When Jesus returned to the temple courts and began to teach, the chief priests and elders of the people came up to Him. “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You this authority?”
units.rightText: And when he was come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came unto him as he was teaching, and said, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority?

units.leftText: “I will also ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said unto them, I also will ask you one question, which if ye tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.

units.leftText: What was the source of John’s baptism? Was it from heaven or from men?”
units.rightText: The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven or from men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say unto us, Why then did ye not believe him?

units.leftText: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we are afraid of the people, for they all regard John as a prophet.”
units.rightText: But if we shall say, From men; we fear the multitude; for all hold John as a prophet.

units.leftText: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things. The Parable of the Two Sons
units.rightText: And they answered Jesus, and said, We know not. He also said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

units.leftText: But what do you think? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the first one and said, ‘Son, go and work today in the vineyard.’
units.rightText: But what think ye? A man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to-day in the vineyard.

units.leftText: ‘I will not,’ he replied. But later he changed his mind and went.
units.rightText: And he answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented himself, and went.
leftNotes: 21:29 NE and WH But he went.

units.leftText: Then the man went to the second son and told him the same thing. ‘I will, sir,’ he said. But he did not go.
units.rightText: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.

units.leftText: Which of the two did the will of his father?” “The first, ” they answered.
units.rightText: Which of the two did the will of his father? They say, The first. Jesus saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, that the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.
leftNotes: 21:31 NE and WH The latter

units.leftText: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes did. And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him. The Parable of the Wicked Tenants (Mark 12:1–12|MRK 12:1-12*; Luke 20:9–18|LUK 20:9-18*)
units.rightText: For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not; but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye saw it, did not even repent yourselves afterward, that ye might believe him.

units.leftText: Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
units.rightText: Hear another parable: There was a man that was a householder, who planted a vineyard, and set a hedge about it, and digged a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into another country.

units.leftText: When the harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit.
units.rightText: And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, to receive his fruits.

units.leftText: But the tenants seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.
units.rightText: And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.

units.leftText: Again, he sent other servants, more than the first group. But the tenants did the same to them.
units.rightText: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they did unto them in like manner.

units.leftText: Finally, he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
units.rightText: But afterward he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.

units.leftText: But when the tenants saw the son, they said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’
units.rightText: But the husbandmen, when they saw the son, said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and take his inheritance.

units.leftText: So they seized him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
units.rightText: And they took him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard, and killed him.

units.leftText: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard returns, what will he do to those tenants?”
units.rightText: When therefore the lord of the vineyard shall come, what will he do unto those husbandmen?

units.leftText: “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end,” they replied, “and will rent out the vineyard to other tenants who will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time.”
units.rightText: They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will let out the vineyard unto other husbandmen, who shall render him the fruits in their seasons.

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’ ?
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, The same was made the head of the corner; This was from the Lord, And it is marvellous in our eyes?

units.leftText: Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.
units.rightText: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken away from you, and shall be given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.

units.leftText: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed. ”
units.rightText: And he that falleth on this stone shall be broken to pieces: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will scatter him as dust.
leftNotes: 21:44 Tischendorf and some early manuscripts do not include verse 44; see also Luke 20:18|LUK 20:18*.

units.leftText: When the chief priests and Pharisees heard His parables, they knew that Jesus was speaking about them.
units.rightText: And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them.

units.leftText: Although they wanted to arrest Him, they were afraid of the crowds, because the people regarded Him as a prophet.
units.rightText: And when they sought to lay hold on him, they feared the multitudes, because they took him for a prophet.

units.leftText: Once again, Jesus spoke to them in parables:
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and spake again in parables unto them, saying,

units.leftText: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
units.rightText: The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a certain king, who made a marriage feast for his son,

units.leftText: He sent his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet, but they refused to come.
units.rightText: and sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the marriage feast: and they would not come.

units.leftText: Again, he sent other servants and said, ‘Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and fattened cattle have been killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.’
units.rightText: Again he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them that are bidden, Behold, I have made ready my dinner; my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come to the marriage feast.

units.leftText: But they paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business.
units.rightText: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise;

units.leftText: The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.
units.rightText: and the rest laid hold on his servants, and treated them shamefully, and killed them.

units.leftText: The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city.
units.rightText: But the king was wroth; and he sent his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.

units.leftText: Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited were not worthy.
units.rightText: Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they that were bidden were not worthy.

units.leftText: Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find.’
units.rightText: Go ye therefore unto the partings of the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage feast.

units.leftText: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
units.rightText: And those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was filled with guests.

units.leftText: But when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.
units.rightText: But when the king came in to behold the guests, he saw there a man who had not on a wedding-garment:

units.leftText: ‘Friend,’ he asked, ‘how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ But the man was speechless.
units.rightText: and he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding-garment? And he was speechless.

units.leftText: Then the king told the servants, ‘Tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
units.rightText: Then the king said to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and cast him out into the outer darkness; there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: For many are called, but few are chosen.” Paying Taxes to Caesar (Mark 12:13–17|MRK 12:13-17*; Luke 20:19–26|LUK 20:19-26*)
units.rightText: For many are called, but few chosen.

units.leftText: Then the Pharisees went out and conspired to trap Jesus in His words.
units.rightText: Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might ensnare him in his talk.

units.leftText: They sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and that You teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You seek favor from no one, because You pay no attention to external appearance.
units.rightText: And they send to him their disciples, with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, and carest not for any one: for thou regardest not the person of men.

units.leftText: So tell us what You think: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
units.rightText: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cæsar, or not?

units.leftText: But Jesus knew their evil intent and said, “You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?
units.rightText: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why make ye trial of me, ye hypocrites?

units.leftText: Show Me the coin used for the tax.” And they brought Him a denarius.
units.rightText: Show me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a denarius.
leftNotes: 22:19 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: “Whose image is this,” He asked, “and whose inscription?”
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?

units.leftText: “Caesar’s,” they answered. So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
units.rightText: They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things that are Cæsar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.

units.leftText: And when they heard this, they were amazed. So they left Him and went away. The Sadducees and the Resurrection (Mark 12:18–27|MRK 12:18-27*; Luke 20:27–40|LUK 20:27-40*)
units.rightText: And when they heard it, they marvelled, and left him, and went away.

units.leftText: That same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him.
units.rightText: On that day there came to him Sadducees, they that say that there is no resurrection: and they asked him,

units.leftText: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses declared that if a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for him.
units.rightText: saying, Teacher, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
leftNotes: 22:24 Deuteronomy 25:5|DEU 25:5*

units.leftText: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died without having children. So he left his wife to his brother.
units.rightText: Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first married and deceased, and having no seed left his wife unto his brother;

units.leftText: The same thing happened to the second and third brothers, down to the seventh.
units.rightText: in like manner the second also, and the third, unto the seventh.

units.leftText: And last of all, the woman died.
units.rightText: And after them all, the woman died.

units.leftText: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven? For all of them were married to her.”
units.rightText: In the resurrection therefore whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.
units.rightText: But Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.

units.leftText: In the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.
units.rightText: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as angels in heaven.
leftNotes: 22:30 SBL, BYZ, and TR the angels of God

units.leftText: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what God said to you:
units.rightText: But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying,

units.leftText: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’ ? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
units.rightText: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
leftNotes: 22:32 Exodus 3:6|EXO 3:6*

units.leftText: When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching. The Greatest Commandment (Deuteronomy 6:1–19|DEU 6:1-19*; Mark 12:28–34|MRK 12:28-34*)
units.rightText: And when the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.

units.leftText: And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together.
units.rightText: But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, gathered themselves together.

units.leftText: One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question:
units.rightText: And one of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, trying him:

units.leftText: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”
units.rightText: Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?

units.leftText: Jesus declared, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
leftNotes: 22:37 Deuteronomy 6:5|DEU 6:5*

units.leftText: This is the first and greatest commandment.
units.rightText: This is the great and first commandment.

units.leftText: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’
units.rightText: And a second like unto it is this, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
leftNotes: 22:39 Leviticus 19:18|LEV 19:18*

units.leftText: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.” Whose Son Is the Christ? (Mark 12:35–37|MRK 12:35-37*; Luke 20:41–44|LUK 20:41-44*)
units.rightText: On these two commandments the whole law hangeth, and the prophets.

units.leftText: While the Pharisees were assembled, Jesus questioned them:
units.rightText: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,

units.leftText: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” “David’s,” they answered.
units.rightText: saying, What think ye of the Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, The son of David.

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call Him ‘Lord’? For he says:
units.rightText: He saith unto them, How then doth David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,

units.leftText: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’
units.rightText: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, Till I put thine enemies underneath thy feet?

units.leftText: So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?”
units.rightText: If David then calleth him Lord, how is he his son?

units.leftText: No one was able to answer a word, and from that day on no one dared to question Him any further.
units.rightText: And no one was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.

units.leftText: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples:
units.rightText: Then spake Jesus to the multitudes and to his disciples,

units.leftText: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
units.rightText: saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat:

units.leftText: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.
units.rightText: all things therefore whatsoever they bid you, these do and observe: but do not ye after their works; for they say, and do not.

units.leftText: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.
units.rightText: Yea, they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with their finger.
leftNotes: 23:4 SBL, NE, and WH They tie up heavy loads

units.leftText: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.
units.rightText: But all their works they do to be seen of men: for they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,

units.leftText: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues,
units.rightText: and love the chief place at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,

units.leftText: the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.
units.rightText: and the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called of men, Rabbi.
leftNotes: 23:7 Literally and to be called ‘Rabbi’ by men

units.leftText: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
units.rightText: But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your teacher, and all ye are brethren.

units.leftText: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
units.rightText: And call no man your father on the earth: for one is your Father, even he who is in heaven.

units.leftText: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.
units.rightText: Neither be ye called masters: for one is your master, even the Christ.

units.leftText: The greatest among you shall be your servant.
units.rightText: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.

units.leftText: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
units.rightText: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be humbled; and whosoever shall humble himself shall be exalted.

units.leftText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.
units.rightText: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye shut the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye enter not in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering in to enter.
leftNotes: 23:13 BYZ and TR include 14*Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.See Mark 12:40|MRK 12:40* and Luke 20:47.

rightNotes: 23:14 Some authorities insert here, or after v. 12, v. 14 Woe unto you scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you devour widows’ houses, even while for a pretence ye make long prayes: therefore ye shall receive greater condemnation. See Mrk 12:40; Luk 20:47.

units.leftText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are.
units.rightText: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he is become so, ye make him twofold more a son of hell than yourselves.
leftNotes: 23:15 Greek Gehenna; also in verse 33

units.leftText: Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’
units.rightText: Woe unto you, ye blind guides, that say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor.

units.leftText: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?
units.rightText: Ye fools and blind: for which is greater, the gold, or the temple that hath sanctified the gold?

units.leftText: And you say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he is bound by his oath.’
units.rightText: And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gift that is upon it, he is a debtor.

units.leftText: You blind men! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes it sacred?
units.rightText: Ye blind: for which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?

units.leftText: So then, he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
units.rightText: He therefore that sweareth by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things thereon.

units.leftText: And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it.
units.rightText: And he that sweareth by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein.

units.leftText: And he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it.
units.rightText: And he that sweareth by the heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth thereon.

units.leftText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin. But you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.
units.rightText: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye tithe mint and anise and cummin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law, justice, and mercy, and faith: but these ye ought to have done, and not to have left the other undone.

units.leftText: You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.
units.rightText: Ye blind guides, that strain out the gnat, and swallow the camel!
leftNotes: 23:24 See Leviticus 11:4|LEV 11:4* and Leviticus 11:23, where camels and gnats are both forbidden as food.

units.leftText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.
units.rightText: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full from extortion and excess.

units.leftText: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that the outside may become clean as well.
units.rightText: Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first the inside of the cup and of the platter, that the outside thereof may become clean also.
leftNotes: 23:26 NA does not include and dish.

units.leftText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.
units.rightText: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.

units.leftText: In the same way, on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.
units.rightText: Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but inwardly ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

units.leftText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.
units.rightText: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and garnish the tombs of the righteous,

units.leftText: And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’
units.rightText: and say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we should not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.

units.leftText: So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
units.rightText: Wherefore ye witness to yourselves, that ye are sons of them that slew the prophets.

units.leftText: Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers.
units.rightText: Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.
leftNotes: 23:32 Or Go ahead, then, and complete

units.leftText: You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape the sentence of hell?
units.rightText: Ye serpents, ye offspring of vipers, how shall ye escape the judgment of hell?

units.leftText: Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town.
units.rightText: Therefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: some of them shall ye kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute from city to city:

units.leftText: And so upon you will come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.
units.rightText: that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous unto the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom ye slew between the sanctuary and the altar.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation. Lament over Jerusalem (Luke 13:31–35|LUK 13:31-35*)
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.

units.leftText: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
units.rightText: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killeth the prophets, and stoneth them that are sent unto her! how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!

units.leftText: Look, your house is left to you desolate.
units.rightText: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
leftNotes: 23:38 NE and WH do not include desolate.

units.leftText: For I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’ ”
units.rightText: For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

units.leftText: As Jesus left the temple and was walking away, His disciples came up to Him to point out its buildings.
units.rightText: And Jesus went out from the temple, and was going on his way; and his disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.

units.leftText: “Do you see all these things?” He replied. “Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”
units.rightText: But he answered and said unto them, See ye not all these things? verily I say unto you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

units.leftText: While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age?”
units.rightText: And as he sat on the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “See to it that no one deceives you.
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man lead you astray.

units.leftText: For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will deceive many.
units.rightText: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am the Christ; and shall lead many astray.

units.leftText: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but see to it that you are not alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.
units.rightText: And ye shall hear of wars and rumors of wars; see that ye be not troubled: for these things must needs come to pass; but the end is not yet.

units.leftText: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places.
units.rightText: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there shall be famines and earthquakes in divers places.

units.leftText: All these are the beginning of birth pains. Witnessing to All Nations (Mark 13:9–13|MRK 13:9-13*; Luke 21:10–19|LUK 21:10-19*)
units.rightText: But all these things are the beginning of travail.

units.leftText: Then they will deliver you over to be persecuted and killed, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.
units.rightText: Then shall they deliver you up unto tribulation, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all the nations for my name’s sake.

units.leftText: At that time many will fall away and will betray and hate one another,
units.rightText: And then shall many stumble, and shall deliver up one another, and shall hate one another.

units.leftText: and many false prophets will arise and deceive many.
units.rightText: And many false prophets shall arise, and shall lead many astray.

units.leftText: Because of the multiplication of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.
units.rightText: And because iniquity shall be multiplied, the love of the many shall wax cold.

units.leftText: But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.
units.rightText: But he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.

units.leftText: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come. The Abomination of Desolation (Mark 13:14–23|MRK 13:14-23*; Luke 21:20–24|LUK 21:20-24*)
units.rightText: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in the whole world for a testimony unto all the nations; and then shall the end come.

units.leftText: So when you see standing in the holy place ‘the abomination of desolation,’ spoken of by the prophet Daniel (let the reader understand),
units.rightText: When therefore ye see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let him that readeth understand),
leftNotes: 24:15 See Daniel 9:27|DAN 9:27*, Daniel 11:31, and Daniel 12:11.

units.leftText: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
units.rightText: then let them that are in Judæa flee unto the mountains:

units.leftText: Let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve anything from his house.
units.rightText: let him that is on the housetop not go down to take out the things that are in his house:

units.leftText: And let no one in the field return for his cloak.
units.rightText: and let him that is in the field not return back to take his cloak.

units.leftText: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!
units.rightText: But woe unto them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days!

units.leftText: Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.
units.rightText: And pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on a sabbath:

units.leftText: For at that time there will be great tribulation, unseen from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be seen again.
units.rightText: for then shall be great tribulation, such as hath not been from the beginning of the world until now, no, nor ever shall be.

units.leftText: If those days had not been cut short, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.
units.rightText: And except those days had been shortened, no flesh would have been saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.

units.leftText: At that time, if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.
units.rightText: Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is the Christ, or, Here; believe it not.

units.leftText: For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.
units.rightText: For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall show great signs and wonders; so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect.

units.leftText: See, I have told you in advance. The Return of the Son of Man (Mark 13:24–27|MRK 13:24-27*; Luke 21:25–28|LUK 21:25-28*)
units.rightText: Behold, I have told you beforehand.

units.leftText: So if they tell you, ‘There He is, in the wilderness,’ do not go out, or, ‘Here He is, in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
units.rightText: If therefore they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the wilderness; go not forth: Behold, he is in the inner chambers; believe it not.

units.leftText: For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
units.rightText: For as the lightning cometh forth from the east, and is seen even unto the west; so shall be the coming of the Son of man.

units.leftText: Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.
units.rightText: Wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together.

units.leftText: Immediately after the tribulation of those days: ‘The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. ’
units.rightText: But immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
leftNotes: 24:29 Or and the celestial bodies will be shaken; see Isaiah 13:10|ISA 13:10*, Isaiah 34:4, and Joel 2:10.

units.leftText: At that time the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
units.rightText: and then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
leftNotes: 24:30 Or the sky; twice in this verse

units.leftText: And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather His elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other. The Lesson of the Fig Tree (Mark 13:28–31|MRK 13:28-31*; Luke 21:29–33|LUK 21:29-33*)
units.rightText: And he shall send forth his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.

units.leftText: Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.
units.rightText: Now from the fig tree learn her parable: when her branch is now become tender, and putteth forth its leaves, ye know that the summer is nigh;
leftNotes: 24:32 Or this parable

units.leftText: So also, when you see all these things, you will know that He is near, right at the door.
units.rightText: even so ye also, when ye see all these things, know ye that he is nigh, even at the doors.
leftNotes: 24:33 Or it is near

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all these things be accomplished.

units.leftText: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away. Readiness at Any Hour (Genesis 6:1–7|GEN 6:1-7*; Mark 13:32–37|MRK 13:32-37*; Luke 12:35–48|LUK 12:35-48*)
units.rightText: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

units.leftText: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
units.rightText: But of that day and hour knoweth no one, not even the angels of heaven, neither the Son, but the Father only.
leftNotes: 24:36 BYZ and TR do not include nor the Son.

units.leftText: As it was in the days of Noah, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.
units.rightText: And as were the days of Noah, so shall be the coming of the Son of man.

units.leftText: For in the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark.
units.rightText: For as in those days which were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark,

units.leftText: And they were oblivious until the flood came and swept them all away. So will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.
units.rightText: and they knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall be the coming of the Son of man.

units.leftText: Two men will be in the field: one will be taken and the other left.
units.rightText: Then shall two men be in the field; one is taken, and one is left:

units.leftText: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and the other left.
units.rightText: two women shall be grinding at the mill; one is taken, and one is left.

units.leftText: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day on which your Lord will come.
units.rightText: Watch therefore: for ye know not on what day your Lord cometh.

units.leftText: But understand this: If the homeowner had known in which watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be broken into.
units.rightText: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken through.

units.leftText: For this reason, you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
units.rightText: Therefore be ye also ready; for in an hour that ye think not the Son of man cometh.

units.leftText: Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom the master has put in charge of his household, to give the others their food at the proper time?
units.rightText: Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath set over his household, to give them their food in due season?

units.leftText: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.
units.rightText: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
