units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, that he will set him over all that he hath.

units.leftText: But suppose that servant is wicked and says in his heart, ‘My master will be away a long time.’
units.rightText: But if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord tarrieth;

units.leftText: And he begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards.
units.rightText: and shall begin to beat his fellow-servants, and shall eat and drink with the drunken;

units.leftText: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate.
units.rightText: the lord of that servant shall come in a day when he expecteth not, and in an hour when he knoweth not,

units.leftText: Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.[’’]
units.rightText: and shall cut him asunder, and appoint his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: “At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
units.rightText: Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, who took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.

units.leftText: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
units.rightText: And five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

units.leftText: The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take along any extra oil.
units.rightText: For the foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them:

units.leftText: But the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.
units.rightText: but the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.

units.leftText: When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
units.rightText: Now while the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept.

units.leftText: At midnight the cry rang out: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’
units.rightText: But at midnight there is a cry, Behold, the bridegroom! Come ye forth to meet him.

units.leftText: Then all the virgins woke up and trimmed their lamps.
units.rightText: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.

units.leftText: The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’
units.rightText: And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are going out.

units.leftText: ‘No,’ said the wise ones, ‘or there may not be enough for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’
units.rightText: But the wise answered, saying, Peradventure there will not be enough for us and you: go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.

units.leftText: But while they were on their way to buy it, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.
units.rightText: And while they went away to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage feast: and the door was shut.

units.leftText: Later the other virgins arrived and said, ‘Lord, lord, open the door for us!’
units.rightText: Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us.

units.leftText: But he replied, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’
units.rightText: But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.

units.leftText: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour. The Parable of the Talents (Luke 19:11–27|LUK 19:11-27*)
units.rightText: Watch therefore, for ye know not the day nor the hour.
leftNotes: 25:13 BYZ and TR include when the Son of Man comes.

units.leftText: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted them with his possessions.
units.rightText: For it is as when a man, going into another country, called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.

units.leftText: To one he gave five talents, to another two talents, and to another one talent — each according to his own ability. And he went on his journey.
units.rightText: And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one; to each according to his several ability; and he went on his journey.
leftNotes: 25:15 A talent was worth about twenty years’ wages for a laborer.

units.leftText: The servant who had received the five talents went at once and put them to work and gained five more.
units.rightText: Straightway he that received the five talents went and traded with them, and made other five talents.
leftNotes: 25:16 Or 15*... And he went on his journey at once. 16*... went and put them to work. Translators vary as to the placement of the Greek adverb eutheōs (at once) at the end of verse 15 or at the beginning of verse 16.

units.leftText: Likewise, the one with the two talents gained two more.
units.rightText: In like manner he also that received the two gained other two.

units.leftText: But the servant who had received the one talent went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.
units.rightText: But he that received the one went away and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.

units.leftText: After a long time the master of those servants returned and settled accounts with them.
units.rightText: Now after a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and maketh a reckoning with them.

units.leftText: The servant who had received the five talents came and presented five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more.’
units.rightText: And he that received the five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents: lo, I have gained other five talents.

units.leftText: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’
units.rightText: His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will set thee over many things; enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

units.leftText: The servant who had received the two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with two talents. See, I have gained two more.’
units.rightText: And he also that received the two talents came and said, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me two talents: lo, I have gained other two talents.

units.leftText: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’
units.rightText: His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will set thee over many things; enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

units.leftText: Finally, the servant who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew that you are a hard man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed.
units.rightText: And he also that had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art a hard man, reaping where thou didst not sow, and gathering where thou didst not scatter;

units.leftText: So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what belongs to you.’
units.rightText: and I was afraid, and went away and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, thou hast thine own.

units.leftText: ‘You wicked, lazy servant!’ replied his master. ‘You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed.
units.rightText: But his lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I did not scatter;

units.leftText: Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my return I would have received it back with interest.
units.rightText: thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the bankers, and at my coming I should have received back mine own with interest.

units.leftText: Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.
units.rightText: Take ye away therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him that hath the ten talents.

units.leftText: For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
units.rightText: For unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not, even that which he hath shall be taken away.

units.leftText: And throw that worthless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’ The Sheep and the Goats
units.rightText: And cast ye out the unprofitable servant into the outer darkness: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, He will sit on His glorious throne.
units.rightText: But when the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the angels with him, then shall he sit on the throne of his glory:

units.leftText: All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
units.rightText: and before him shall be gathered all the nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as the shepherd separateth the sheep from the goats;

units.leftText: He will place the sheep on His right and the goats on His left.
units.rightText: and he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.

units.leftText: Then the King will say to those on His right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
units.rightText: Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:

units.leftText: For I was hungry and you gave Me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me something to drink, I was a stranger and you took Me in,
units.rightText: for I was hungry, and ye gave me to eat; I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink; I was a stranger, and ye took me in;

units.leftText: I was naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you looked after Me, I was in prison and you visited Me.’
units.rightText: naked, and ye clothed me; I was sick, and ye visited me; I was in prison, and ye came unto me.

units.leftText: Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You something to drink?
units.rightText: Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee hungry, and fed thee? or athirst, and gave thee drink?

units.leftText: When did we see You a stranger and take You in, or naked and clothe You?
units.rightText: And when saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee?

units.leftText: When did we see You sick or in prison and visit You?’
units.rightText: And when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee?

units.leftText: And the King will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me.’
units.rightText: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it unto one of these my brethren, even these least, ye did it unto me.

units.leftText: Then He will say to those on His left, ‘Depart from Me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
units.rightText: Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels:

units.leftText: For I was hungry and you gave Me nothing to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me nothing to drink,
units.rightText: for I was hungry, and ye did not give me to eat; I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink;

units.leftText: I was a stranger and you did not take Me in, I was naked and you did not clothe Me, I was sick and in prison and you did not look after Me.’
units.rightText: I was a stranger, and ye took me not in; naked, and ye clothed me not; sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not.

units.leftText: And they too will reply, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?’
units.rightText: Then shall they also answer, saying, Lord, when saw we thee hungry, or athirst, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister unto thee?

units.leftText: Then the King will answer, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me.’
units.rightText: Then shall he answer them, saying, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not unto one of these least, ye did it not unto me.

units.leftText: And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
units.rightText: And these shall go away into eternal punishment: but the righteous into eternal life.

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished saying all these things, He told His disciples,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these words, he said unto his disciples,

units.leftText: “You know that the Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
units.rightText: Ye know that after two days the passover cometh, and the Son of man is delivered up to be crucified.

units.leftText: At that time the chief priests and elders of the people assembled in the courtyard of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas,
units.rightText: Then were gathered together the chief priests, and the elders of the people, unto the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas;

units.leftText: and they conspired to arrest Jesus covertly and kill Him.
units.rightText: and they took counsel together that they might take Jesus by subtlety, and kill him.

units.leftText: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.” Jesus Anointed at Bethany (Mark 14:3–9|MRK 14:3-9*; Luke 7:36–50|LUK 7:36-50*; John 12:1–8|JHN 12:1-8*)
units.rightText: But they said, Not during the feast, lest a tumult arise among the people.

units.leftText: While Jesus was in Bethany in the home of Simon the Leper,
units.rightText: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
leftNotes: 26:6 Aramaic Simon the Potter or Simon the Jar Maker

units.leftText: a woman came to Him with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, which she poured on His head as He reclined at the table.
units.rightText: there came unto him a woman having an alabaster cruse of exceeding precious ointment, and she poured it upon his head, as he sat at meat.

units.leftText: When the disciples saw this, they were indignant and asked, “Why this waste?
units.rightText: But when the disciples saw it, they had indignation, saying, To what purpose is this waste?

units.leftText: This perfume could have been sold at a high price, and the money given to the poor.”
units.rightText: For this ointment might have been sold for much, and given to the poor.

units.leftText: Aware of this, Jesus asked, “Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.
units.rightText: But Jesus perceiving it said unto them, Why trouble ye the woman? for she hath wrought a good work upon me.

units.leftText: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.
units.rightText: For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.
leftNotes: 26:11 See Deuteronomy 15:11|DEU 15:11*.

units.leftText: By pouring this perfume on Me, she has prepared My body for burial.
units.rightText: For in that she poured this ointment upon my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.” Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus (Mark 14:10–11|MRK 14:10-11*; Luke 22:3–6|LUK 22:3-6*)
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, that also which this woman hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.

units.leftText: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
units.rightText: Then one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests,

units.leftText: and asked, “What are you willing to give me if I hand Him over to you?” And they set out for him thirty pieces of silver.
units.rightText: and said, What are ye willing to give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they weighed unto him thirty pieces of silver.

units.leftText: So from then on Judas looked for an opportunity to betray Jesus. Preparing the Passover (Mark 14:12–16|MRK 14:12-16*; Luke 22:7–13|LUK 22:7-13*)
units.rightText: And from that time he sought opportunity to deliver him unto them.

units.leftText: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”
units.rightText: Now on the first day of unleavened bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying, Where wilt thou that we make ready for thee to eat the passover?
leftNotes: 26:17 Literally On the first of the Unleavened; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.

units.leftText: He answered, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him that the Teacher says, ‘My time is near. I will keep the Passover with My disciples at your house.’”
units.rightText: And he said, Go into the city to such a man, and say unto him, The Teacher saith, My time is at hand; I keep the passover at thy house with my disciples.

units.leftText: So the disciples did as Jesus had directed them and prepared the Passover. The Last Supper (Mark 14:17–26|MRK 14:17-26*; Luke 22:14–23|LUK 22:14-23*; 1 Corinthians 11:17–34|1CO 11:17-34*)
units.rightText: And the disciples did as Jesus appointed them; and they made ready the passover.

units.leftText: When evening came, Jesus was reclining with the twelve disciples.
units.rightText: Now when even was come, he was sitting at meat with the twelve disciples;
leftNotes: 26:20 BYZ and TR the Twelve

units.leftText: And while they were eating, He said to them, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”
units.rightText: and as they were eating, he said, Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.

units.leftText: They were deeply grieved and began to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I, Lord?”
units.rightText: And they were exceeding sorrowful, and began to say unto him every one, Is it I, Lord?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with Me will betray Me.
units.rightText: And he answered and said, He that dipped his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me.

units.leftText: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed. It would be better for him if he had not been born.”
units.rightText: The Son of man goeth, even as it is written of him: but woe unto that man through whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had not been born.

units.leftText: Then Judas, who would betray Him, said, “Surely not I, Rabbi?” Jesus answered, “You have said it yourself.”
units.rightText: And Judas, who betrayed him, answered and said, Is it I, Rabbi? He saith unto him, Thou hast said.

units.leftText: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is My body.”
units.rightText: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed, and brake it; and he gave to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.

units.leftText: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.
units.rightText: And he took a cup, and gave thanks, and gave to them, saying, Drink ye all of it;

units.leftText: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
units.rightText: for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many unto remission of sins.
leftNotes: 26:28 BYZ and TR the new covenant

units.leftText: I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father’s kingdom.”
units.rightText: But I say unto you, I shall not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.

units.leftText: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives. Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial (Zechariah 13:7–9|ZEC 13:7-9*; Mark 14:27–31|MRK 14:27-31*; Luke 22:31–38|LUK 22:31-38*; John 13:36–38|JHN 13:36-38*)
units.rightText: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to them, “This very night you will all fall away on account of Me. For it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
units.rightText: Then saith Jesus unto them, All ye shall be offended in me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.
leftNotes: 26:31 Zechariah 13:7|ZEC 13:7*

units.leftText: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
units.rightText: But after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.

units.leftText: Peter said to Him, “Even if all fall away on account of You, I never will.”
units.rightText: But Peter answered and said unto him, If all shall be offended in thee, I will never be offended.

units.leftText: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus declared, “this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”
units.rightText: Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, that this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

units.leftText: Peter replied, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the other disciples said the same thing. Jesus Prays at Gethsemane (Mark 14:32–42|MRK 14:32-42*; Luke 22:39–46|LUK 22:39-46*)
units.rightText: Peter saith unto him, Even if I must die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Likewise also said all the disciples.

units.leftText: Then Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and He told them, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
units.rightText: Then cometh Jesus with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto his disciples, Sit ye here, while I go yonder and pray.

units.leftText: He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee and began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed.
units.rightText: And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and sore troubled.

units.leftText: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”
units.rightText: Then saith he unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: abide ye here, and watch with me.

units.leftText: Going a little farther, He fell facedown and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Yet not as I will, but as You will.”
units.rightText: And he went forward a little, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, My Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass away from me: nevertheless, not as I will, but as thou wilt.

units.leftText: Then Jesus returned to the disciples and found them sleeping. “Were you not able to keep watch with Me for one hour?” He asked Peter.
units.rightText: And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them sleeping, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?

units.leftText: “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
units.rightText: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

units.leftText: A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”
units.rightText: Again a second time he went away, and prayed, saying, My Father, if this cannot pass away, except I drink it, thy will be done.

units.leftText: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
units.rightText: And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.

units.leftText: So He left them and went away once more and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.
units.rightText: And he left them again, and went away, and prayed a third time, saying again the same words.

units.leftText: Then He returned to the disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
units.rightText: Then cometh he to the disciples, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

units.leftText: Rise, let us go! See, My betrayer is approaching!” The Betrayal of Jesus (Mark 14:43–52|MRK 14:43-52*; Luke 22:47–53|LUK 22:47-53*; John 18:1–14|JHN 18:1-14*)
units.rightText: Arise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that betrayeth me.

units.leftText: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and elders of the people.
units.rightText: And while he yet spake, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

units.leftText: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him.”
units.rightText: Now he that betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that is he: take him.

units.leftText: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
units.rightText: And straightway he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, Rabbi; and kissed him.

units.leftText: “Friend,” Jesus replied, “do what you came for.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, Friend, do that for which thou art come. Then they came and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.
leftNotes: 26:50 Or “Friend,” Jesus replied, “for what have you come?”

units.leftText: At this, one of Jesus’ companions drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
units.rightText: And behold, one of them that were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and smote the servant of the high priest, and struck off his ear.

units.leftText: “Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him. “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.
units.rightText: Then saith Jesus unto him, Put up again thy sword into its place: for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.

units.leftText: Are you not aware that I can call on My Father, and He will at once put at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels?
units.rightText: Or thinkest thou that I cannot beseech my Father, and he shall even now send me more than twelve legions of angels?

units.leftText: But how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that say it must happen this way?”
units.rightText: How then should the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be?

units.leftText: At that time Jesus said to the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw? Every day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me.
units.rightText: In that hour said Jesus to the multitudes, Are ye come out as against a robber with swords and staves to seize me? I sat daily in the temple teaching, and ye took me not.
leftNotes: 26:55 Literally the temple

units.leftText: But this has all happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples deserted Him and fled. Jesus before the Sanhedrin (Mark 14:53–65|MRK 14:53-65*; Luke 22:66–71|LUK 22:66-71*; John 18:19–24|JHN 18:19-24*)
units.rightText: But all this is come to pass, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples left him, and fled.

units.leftText: Those who had arrested Jesus led Him away to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
units.rightText: And they that had taken Jesus led him away to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.
